definition_zh: 着迷；魅力；吸引力；令人着迷的事物
definition_en: a strong interest or attraction that holds the mind
core_image: 磁石下的铁屑：目光和心神都被吸过去
scene: 博物馆里那具古老的遗体让参观者既害怕又挪不开眼。The ancient body in the museum held the visitors in a mixture of fear and fascination.
sceneCN: 这里 fascination 是「着迷；入迷」（第 1 个义项：被某物强烈吸引而移不开注意的状态）；句意：博物馆里那具古老的遗体让参观者既害怕又挪不开眼。

derivatives.zh: 使着迷；强烈吸引
迷人的；极有吸引力的
着迷的；被吸引的

senses.title: A state of intense attraction
senses.definition: the state of being strongly attracted or absorbed by something
senses.definitionCN: 被某物强烈吸引、全神贯注的状态
senses.example: She watched the dancer with fascination.
senses.exampleCN: 她着迷地看着那位舞者。
senses.why: The Latin source is a spell, and this first sense is the spell at work: attention is caught and held.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词源是「符咒」，第一个义项就是符咒生效：注意力被抓住并固定住。

senses.title: The power to attract
senses.definition: the quality of being extremely interesting or attractive
senses.definitionCN: 极其有趣或吸引人的特质
senses.example: The old city has a fascination that never fades.
senses.exampleCN: 这座古城有一种永不消退的魅力。
senses.why: A spell can also live in the thing itself, so the word comes to name the charm it radiates.
senses.whyCN: 符咒也可以附着在事物本身，于是这个词转而指事物散发出的魅力。

senses.title: An object of intense interest
senses.definition: a person or thing that draws intense and lasting interest
senses.definitionCN: 引起强烈而持久兴趣的人或物
senses.example: The lost ship became a fascination for treasure hunters.
senses.exampleCN: 那艘失踪的船成了寻宝者着迷的对象。
senses.why: What casts a spell can also be the thing watched, so the spell is transferred to its target.
senses.whyCN: 施咒之物也可以是被凝视的对象，于是「魔力」被转移到被吸引的目标上。

senses.title: Bewitchment by magic
senses.definition: the condition of being controlled by a spell, in older usage
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法中被符咒控制的状态
senses.example: The villagers feared the wanderer and his strange fascination.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们害怕那个流浪者和他古怪的蛊惑之力。
senses.why: The oldest sense is literal enchantment: a spell that takes away the will.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是字面的「中邪」：符咒夺走了人的意志。

intro.en: Fascination comes from Latin fascinatio, a bewitching, from fascinare, to enchant, and fascinum, a spell or charm.
intro.cn: fascination 来自拉丁语 fascinatio（迷惑、施魔法），源于 fascinare（施魔法）与 fascinum（符咒、魔力）。

items.en: Fascinum names a spell, a charm, or a bewitched object.
items.cn: fascinum 指符咒、魔力或受咒之物。

items.en: Fascinare means to bewitch or to put someone under a spell.
items.cn: fascinare 意为施魔法或使某人中邪。

items.en: Fascinatio is the act of bewitching or the state of being bewitched.
items.cn: fascinatio 指施魔法的动作或中邪的状态。

items.en: English borrows the word for the state of being enchanted or charmed.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入该词，指中邪或被迷住的状态。

items.en: The sense softens into strong, often admiring interest.
items.cn: 现代英语中语义变柔，多指强烈而常带欣赏的兴趣。

note.en: Fascination is the spell of attraction, close to its verb family and to words for allure.
note.cn: fascination 是「吸引之咒」，与它的动词词族以及表示诱惑的词相邻。

entries.definition: to attract and hold the attention of
extremely interesting or attractive
deeply interested or attracted
the quality of being powerfully attractive
a pleasing quality that attracts people
a strong, often unhealthy, interest in something

normalIntro.en: Fascination keeps the image of a spell: something outside the self takes hold of attention.
normalIntro.cn: fascination 保留「符咒」的意象：身外之物攫住了注意力。

normal.en: Fascination and fascinate share one Latin root.
normal.cn: fascination 与 fascinate 共享同一个拉丁词根。

normal.en: The verb fascinate means to hold attention completely.
normal.cn: 动词 fascinate 意为完全抓住注意力。

normal.en: A fascinating thing has the power to pull people in.
normal.cn: fascinating 的事物有把人吸进去的力量。

normal.en: To watch in fascination is to watch without looking away.
normal.cn: in fascination 地看，就是看得目不转睛。

normal.en: Compare interest: interest is mild, fascination is intense.
normal.cn: 对比 interest：interest 较温和，fascination 更强烈。

abstract.en: Picture iron filings leaping toward a magnet.
abstract.cn: 想象铁屑朝磁石跳过去。

abstract.en: Imagine a lantern in a dark room: you cannot look elsewhere.
abstract.cn: 想象暗室里的一盏灯：你无法看向别处。

abstract.en: Think of a rare shell that keeps divers returning.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚稀有贝壳，让潜水者一再回来。

examples.en: Her fascination with ancient maps began in childhood.
examples.cn: 她从小就对古地图着迷。

examples.en: The dark cave exercises a strange fascination over visitors.
examples.cn: 那座黑暗的洞穴对游客有一种奇怪的吸引力。

examples.en: He listened to the lecture with growing fascination.
examples.cn: 他越听讲座越着迷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fascination」可拆成「fasci + nation」——联想「一整个 nation 都被吸住」；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 fascinum（符咒、魔力）→ fascinare（施魔法）→ fascinatio（迷惑）→ 英语 fascination，核心义「被魔力吸住」。

sensesIntro.en: Fascination starts as the effect of a spell, then names the charm itself, then the thing that charms, and finally literal bewitchment.
sensesIntro.cn: fascination 先指符咒产生的效果，再指魅力本身，继而指施魅之物，最后保留字面的「中邪」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a magnet pulling eyes and mind toward it.
core.cn: 核心意象：磁石把目光与心神一起吸过去。

branches.en: Being absorbed is the state sense.
branches.cn: 全神贯注是被吸引的状态义项。

branches.en: The attractive quality is the charm sense.
branches.cn: 吸引人的特质是魅力义项。

branches.en: The thing that draws interest is the object sense.
branches.cn: 引发兴趣的对象是客体义项。

branches.en: A charm works by producing the state of fascination.
branches.cn: 魅力正是通过制造着迷状态而发挥作用。

branches.en: An odd object can be both a fascination and a feared spell.
branches.cn: 古怪之物既可能是着迷对象，也可能是令人畏惧的符咒。

intro.en: Fascination belongs to a Latin family of spell words, with fascinate and fascinating built beside it.
intro.cn: fascination 属于拉丁语「符咒」词族，旁边有 fascinate 与 fascinating。

latinIntro.en: Latin fascinum is a spell, fascinare is to bewitch, and fascinatio is a bewitching.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fascinum 是符咒，fascinare 是施魔法，fascinatio 是迷惑。

items.example: Fascinum names the object that carries magic.
items.exampleCN: fascinum 指承载魔力的物件。

items.example: Fascinare is the act of casting a spell.
items.exampleCN: fascinare 是施符咒的动作。

items.example: Fascinatio is the direct source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: fascinatio 是英语名词的直接来源。

items.example: Fascinate keeps the verb sense of the family.
items.exampleCN: fascinate 保留这个词族的动词义。

items.example: Fascinating describes the power to hold attention.
items.exampleCN: fascinating 描述抓住注意力的力量。

items.example: Fascinated describes the person who is held.
items.exampleCN: fascinated 描述被吸住的人。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或状态的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms fascination from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 由动词构成 fascination。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms fascinating.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 fascinating。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms fascinated.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 fascinated。

definition_zh: 紧固件；扣件；拉链；夹子
definition_en: a device that closes, joins, or holds something firmly
core_image: 一枚搭扣：两片材料被牢牢扣在一起
scene: 她拉上外套的拉链，又按了按每一枚扣子。She pulled up the zip and pressed every fastener on her coat.
sceneCN: 这里 fastener 是「扣合件」（第 1 个义项：衣服上用来扣合的东西）；句意：她拉上外套的拉链，又按了按每一枚扣子。

derivatives.zh: 系紧；扣紧
扣合；紧固件
解开；松开

senses.title: A closure on clothing
senses.definition: a button, zip, or clasp that closes clothing
senses.definitionCN: 扣住衣服的纽扣、拉链或搭扣
senses.example: The coat has a broken fastener at the collar.
senses.exampleCN: 这件外套领口的扣件坏了。
senses.why: Fasten means to make firm, so a fastener is the small thing that makes cloth stay closed.
senses.whyCN: fasten 意为使牢固，fastener 就是让衣物保持扣合的小物件。

senses.title: Hardware that joins parts
senses.definition: a bolt, screw, rivet, or similar piece used to hold structures together
senses.definitionCN: 用于把结构件固定在一起的螺栓、螺钉、铆钉等
senses.example: Workers checked every steel fastener on the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 工人检查了桥上的每一枚钢制紧固件。
senses.why: The agent suffix -er turns the action of fastening into an object that does the fastening.
senses.whyCN: 施事后缀 -er 把「紧固」这一动作变成执行紧固的物件。

senses.title: A clip or pin for loose material
senses.definition: a clip, pin, or similar item that holds papers or fabric in place
senses.definitionCN: 夹住纸张或布料的夹子、别针一类物件
senses.example: She used a paper fastener to hold the pages together.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一枚夹纸钉把书页夹在一起。
senses.why: Any small device that fastens loose material inherits the same core idea of holding things firm.
senses.whyCN: 任何把松散材料固定住的小器件，都继承了「使东西牢固」的核心义。

intro.en: Fastener is an English agent noun from fasten, which comes from Old English fæstan and the adjective fæst, firm.
intro.cn: fastener 是英语由 fasten 构成的施事名词；fasten 来自古英语 fæstan 与形容词 fæst（牢固的）。

items.en: The reconstructed adjective fastuz means firm or fixed.
items.cn: 重构形容词 fastuz 意为牢固的、固定的。

items.en: Fæst means firm, and fæstan means to make firm or secure.
items.cn: 古英语 fæst 意为牢固，fæstan 意为使牢固、系紧。

items.en: Fasten carries the verb into Middle English with the sense to secure.
items.cn: fasten 进入中古英语，保留「使牢固」的动词义。

items.en: The agent noun fastener appears, first naming a person who fastens.
items.cn: 施事名词 fastener 出现，最初指做紧固工作的人。

items.en: The word shifts to the device itself and expands to bolts, zips, and clips.
items.cn: 词义转向器件本身，并扩展到螺栓、拉链与夹子。

note.en: Fastener is the thing that fastens, next to its verb family and to other closure words.
note.cn: fastener 是「使牢固的物件」，与它的动词词族以及其他扣合类词相邻。

entries.definition: to close or join something firmly
a device or act that closes something
to open or release something closed
a device that holds two parts together
a metal or plastic closure with a tongue
a small bar that keeps a door or gate closed

normalIntro.en: Fastener is built from fasten plus -er: the little thing that makes something fast.
normalIntro.cn: fastener 由 fasten 加 -er 构成：那个让东西牢固的小物件。

normal.en: Fasten means to make firm or secure.
normal.cn: fasten 意为使牢固、系紧。

normal.en: A fastener is the object that does the fastening.
normal.cn: fastener 就是执行紧固的物件。

normal.en: A zip fastener closes a jacket in one pull.
normal.cn: zip fastener 一拉就扣住夹克。

normal.en: A paper fastener holds loose pages together.
normal.cn: paper fastener 把散页夹在一起。

normal.en: Compare fast: fast as an adjective means firm or fixed.
normal.cn: 对比 fast：fast 作形容词意为牢固的、固定的。

abstract.en: Picture a coat button clicking shut.
abstract.cn: 想象外套扣子咔哒扣上。

abstract.en: Imagine a bolt pulled tight through two steel plates.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚螺栓穿过两块钢板被拧紧。

abstract.en: Think of a paper clip biting a stack of pages.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚回形针咬住一叠纸。

examples.en: The fastener on my bag broke on the train.
examples.cn: 我包上的扣件在火车上坏了。

examples.en: Engineers replaced the steel fasteners before winter.
examples.cn: 工程师在入冬前更换了钢制紧固件。

examples.en: She chose a coat with a simple fastener.
examples.cn: 她选了一件扣合简单的女式外套。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fastener」可拆成 fast（牢固）+ en + er（物）——让东西牢固的物件；这只是拆词联想，不是词源考据。

root: 古英语 fæst（牢固的）→ fæstan（使牢固）→ 中古英语 fasten → fasten + -er（表物）→ fastener，核心义「使东西牢固的物件」。

sensesIntro.en: Fastener begins as a person who fastens, then becomes the device on clothes, in machinery, and on loose papers.
sensesIntro.cn: fastener 最初指做紧固工作的人，后来指衣服、机械与散页上的各种扣合器件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clasp pulling two edges tightly together.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚搭扣把两边紧紧拉在一起。

branches.en: A clothing closure is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 衣服上的扣合件是日常义项。

branches.en: Industrial hardware is the mechanical sense.
branches.cn: 工业紧固件是机械义项。

branches.en: A clip for papers is the small-object sense.
branches.cn: 夹纸的夹子是小物件义项。

branches.en: Both buttons and clips keep loose things from separating.
branches.cn: 纽扣与夹子都防止松散之物分开。

branches.en: A bolt and a paper fastener both work by holding parts together.
branches.cn: 螺栓与夹纸钉都靠把部件固定在一起而发挥作用。

intro.en: Fastener is a Germanic English word; its family grows through fasten, fastening, and unfasten rather than through Latin roots.
intro.cn: fastener 是日耳曼语源的英语词，其词族经由 fasten、fastening 与 unfasten 扩展，而非拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor for fastener; the word traces back to Old English fæst and fæstan.
latinIntro.cn: fastener 没有拉丁语祖先，可追溯到古英语 fæst 与 fæstan。

items.example: Fæst is the adjective behind fasten.
items.exampleCN: fæst 是 fasten 背后的形容词。

items.example: Fæstan is the direct verb ancestor.
items.exampleCN: fæstan 是直接的动词祖先。

items.example: Fasten is the modern verb.
items.exampleCN: fasten 是现代英语动词。

items.example: Fastener is the noun built with -er.
items.exampleCN: fastener 是加 -er 构成的名词。

items.meaning: a closure or the act of closing
items.example: Fastening names both the act and the thing.
items.exampleCN: fastening 同时指动作与物件。

items.example: Unfasten adds the negative prefix un-.
items.exampleCN: unfasten 加了否定前缀 un-。

items.example: Fast keeps the old sense of firm.
items.exampleCN: fast 保留「牢固」的旧义。

items.meaning: one who or that which does
items.meaningCN: 表示做某事的人或物的词尾
items.example: The suffix -er forms fastener from fasten.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 由 fasten 构成 fastener。

items.example: Fastener tape is a modern closure.
items.exampleCN: fastener tape 是一种现代扣合材料。

definition_zh: 决定命运的；重大的；带来灾难的；不祥的
definition_en: having an important, often bad, effect on what happens later
core_image: 命运女神手中的线：一剪下去，人生改道
scene: 他在那个清晨签下了一份改变一生的文件。On that morning he signed a fateful document that changed his life.
sceneCN: 这里 fateful 是「决定命运的」（第 1 个义项：对以后有决定性影响的）；句意：他在那个清晨签下了一份改变一生的文件。

pos.zh: 决定命运的；重大的；带来灾难的

derivatives.zh: 命运；天意
命中注定的
决定命运地
决定性；重大性

senses.title: Decisive for the future
senses.definition: having a decisive effect on what happens later
senses.definitionCN: 对后来发生的事有决定性影响
senses.example: That summer proved fateful for the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 那个夏天对整个家庭来说成了决定命运的转折。
senses.why: Fate is what has been spoken and fixed, so a fateful event is one that fixes the future.
senses.whyCN: fate 是「已被说出并定下的事」，因此 fateful 的事件就是替未来定调的事件。

senses.title: Bringing disaster or death
senses.definition: bringing serious harm, ruin, or death
senses.definitionCN: 带来严重伤害、毁灭或死亡
senses.example: The fateful storm destroyed the harbor in one night.
senses.exampleCN: 那场灾难性的风暴一夜之间摧毁了港口。
senses.why: A decisive turn can be terrible, so the word takes on the sense of a disastrous outcome.
senses.whyCN: 决定性的转折也可能是可怕的，于是这个词带上「灾难性结果」的含义。

senses.title: Ominous in older use
senses.definition: warning of something bad that is going to happen, in older or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 旧时或文学用法中预示坏事将要发生
senses.example: They saw a fateful omen in the broken mirror.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在破碎的镜子里看到了不祥的征兆。
senses.why: The oldest layer is prophecy: a fateful thing announces what fate has already decreed.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的一层是预言：fateful 之物宣告命运已经注定的事。

intro.en: Fateful joins fate, from Latin fatum, with the suffix -ful. Fatum means what has been spoken, from fari, to speak.
intro.cn: fateful 由 fate 加后缀 -ful 构成；fate 来自拉丁语 fatum，意为「被说出的话」，源于 fari（说话）。

items.en: Fari means to speak or pronounce.
items.cn: fari 意为说话、宣告。

items.en: Fatum is what has been spoken, hence a divine decree or destiny.
items.cn: fatum 是「被说出的东西」，引申为神谕或命运。

items.en: Old French fate carries the word toward English, alongside direct borrowing from Latin.
items.cn: 古法语 fate 把该词带向英语，同时英语也直接从拉丁语借入。

items.en: Fate appears in English around the fourteenth century.
items.cn: fate 约在十四世纪进入英语。

items.en: The adjective fateful is formed with -ful, meaning full of fate or prophetic.
items.cn: 形容词 fateful 由 -ful 构成，意为「充满命运的」或「预言的」。

items.en: The modern sense settles on decisive and often disastrous consequences.
items.cn: 现代义固定为「决定性的、且常为灾难性的后果」。

note.en: Fateful is fate plus -ful, close to its fate family and to adjectives for decisive or disastrous events.
note.cn: fateful 是 fate 加 -ful，与 fate 词族以及表示决定性、灾难性事件的形容词相邻。

entries.definition: the power that decides what happens
decided by fate
causing death or ruin
settling an issue or a future course
entries.definitionCN: 决定性的；起决定作用的

entries.definition: suggesting that something bad will happen
causing great harm or failure

normalIntro.en: Fateful is fate with -ful: a moment that is full of fate and fixes what follows.
normalIntro.cn: fateful 是 fate 加 -ful：一个装满命运、定下后续走向的时刻。

normal.en: Fate comes from Latin fatum, something spoken and fixed.
normal.cn: fate 来自拉丁语 fatum，即被说出并定下的事。

normal.en: The suffix -ful means full of, as in fateful.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ful 意为「充满……的」，fateful 即「充满命运的」。

normal.en: A fateful decision changes the course of later events.
normal.cn: fateful decision 会改变后续事件的走向。

normal.en: A fateful day often ends in loss or ruin.
normal.cn: fateful day 常以损失或毁灭收场。

normal.en: Compare fatal: fatal means causing death, fateful means decisive.
normal.cn: 对比 fatal：fatal 指致命的，fateful 指决定命运的。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of scissors cutting a thread of life.
abstract.cn: 想象一把剪刀剪断生命之线。

abstract.en: Imagine a storm that sinks a ship on the night it sails.
abstract.cn: 想象一场风暴在船启航之夜将其击沉。

abstract.en: Think of a cracked mirror that seems to warn of coming trouble.
abstract.cn: 想象一面裂开的镜子，似乎在预告即将到来的麻烦。

examples.en: That fateful meeting led her to change careers.
examples.cn: 那次决定命运的会面让她转了行。

examples.en: Historians still debate the fateful order to advance.
examples.cn: 历史学家仍在争论那道决定命运的前进命令。

examples.en: He ignored the fateful warning in the words of the old man.
examples.cn: 他忽略了老人话里那不祥的警告。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fateful」可拆成 fate（命运）+ ful（满）——命运装满的时刻；这只是拆词联想，不是词源考据。

root: 拉丁语 fari（说话）→ fatum（被说出的话、命运）→ 古法语 fate → 英语 fate + -ful（充满……的）→ fateful，核心义「装满命运的」。

sensesIntro.en: Fateful moves from a decisive turning point to a disastrous outcome and then to an ominous sign.
sensesIntro.cn: fateful 从决定性的转折点，扩展到灾难性结果，再指不祥的预兆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thread of life cut by fate.
core.cn: 核心意象：命运剪断生命之线。

branches.en: A decisive moment is the core sense.
branches.cn: 决定性的时刻是核心义项。

branches.en: A disastrous outcome is the dark sense.
branches.cn: 灾难性结果是阴暗义项。

branches.en: An omen is the prophetic sense.
branches.cn: 预兆是预言义项。

branches.en: A decisive turn often brings disaster.
branches.cn: 决定性的转折常常带来灾难。

branches.en: Both a decisive hour and an omen point to what fate has fixed.
branches.cn: 决定性的时刻与预兆都指向命运已经定下的事。

intro.en: Fateful is an English formation from fate and -ful; the family also includes fated, fatal, and fatality.
intro.cn: fateful 是英语由 fate 与 -ful 构成的词，同族还有 fated、fatal 与 fatality。

latinIntro.en: Latin fari means to speak, and fatum means what has been spoken or decreed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fari 意为说话，fatum 意为被说出或注定的事。

items.example: Fari is the verb behind fatum.
items.exampleCN: fari 是 fatum 背后的动词。

items.example: Fatum gives English fate.
items.exampleCN: fatum 给出英语 fate。

items.example: Fatalis gives English fatal.
items.exampleCN: fatalis 给出英语 fatal。

items.example: Fate is the noun at the centre of the family.
items.exampleCN: fate 是这个词族的核心名词。

items.meaningCN: 决定命运的；常带灾难的
items.example: Fateful adds the suffix -ful to fate.
items.exampleCN: fateful 在 fate 后加了后缀 -ful。

items.example: Fated describes what cannot be avoided.
items.exampleCN: fated 描述无法避免的事。

items.example: Fatefully modifies the action.
items.exampleCN: fatefully 修饰动作。

items.example: The suffix -ful forms fateful.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ful 构成 fateful。

items.example: Fatality belongs to the same fate family.
items.exampleCN: fatality 属于同一个 fate 词族。

definition_zh: 动物群；动物区系；动物志
definition_en: the animals of a particular region, period, or habitat, taken as a group
core_image: 一张动物名录：同一片土地上的所有动物排成一行
scene: 雨林深处，夜晚的叫声来自无数种动物。Deep in the rainforest, the night calls come from a rich fauna of insects, frogs, and birds.
sceneCN: 这里 fauna 是「动物群」（第 1 个义项：某一地区的全部动物）；句意：雨林深处，夜晚的叫声来自无数种动物。

pos.zh: 动物群；动物区系；动物志

derivatives.zh: 动物群的；动物区系的
动物区系学的
动物区系研究者

senses.title: The animals of a region
senses.definition: all the animals living in a particular area or period
senses.definitionCN: 生活在某一地区或某一时期的全部动物
senses.example: The island has a unique fauna found nowhere else.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛有独一无二的动物群。
senses.why: Fauna began as the name of a countryside goddess, then became a collective name for the animals of a place.
senses.whyCN: fauna 最初是乡野女神之名，后来成为某地动物全体的集合名称。

senses.title: Animal life as a whole
senses.definition: animal life considered as a group, especially in contrast to plant life
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体来看的动物生命，尤与植物生命相对
senses.example: The survey compares the fauna of the valley with its flora.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查把山谷的动物与植物作比较。
senses.why: Once the word names a collective, it can stand for animal life in general, paired with flora.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词成为集合名词，就能泛指动物生命，并与 flora（植物群）配对。

senses.title: A systematic account of animals
senses.definition: a book or list that describes the animals of a region
senses.definitionCN: 描述某地区动物的书或名录
senses.example: The naturalist published a fauna of the northern lakes.
senses.exampleCN: 那位博物学家出版了北方湖泊的动物志。
senses.why: Scientific titles such as Fauna Suecica turned the word into a name for a catalogue of animals.
senses.whyCN: 《Fauna Suecica》这类科学书名把该词变成动物名录的名称。

intro.en: Fauna comes from the Latin name Fauna, a rural goddess, and was used by Linnaeus as a title for a catalogue of Swedish animals.
intro.cn: fauna 来自拉丁语女神名 Fauna（乡野女神），林奈曾用它作瑞典动物志的书名。

items.en: Fauna is a Roman goddess of the countryside, linked to Faunus.
items.cn: Fauna 是罗马乡野女神，与 Faunus 相关联。

items.en: Faunus is a rural god associated with woods and animals.
items.cn: Faunus 是与树林和动物相关的乡野神。

items.en: Linnaeus uses Fauna Suecica as the title of his catalogue of Swedish animals.
items.cn: 林奈用《Fauna Suecica》作为瑞典动物志的书名。

items.en: English adopts fauna as a collective term for the animals of a region.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪采用 fauna，作为某地区动物的集合术语。

items.en: The word extends to fossil faunas, marine faunas, and habitat studies.
items.cn: 该词扩展到化石动物群、海洋动物群与栖息地研究。

note.en: Fauna is the animal counterpart of flora, close to its Latin name source and to related study words.
note.cn: fauna 是与 flora 相对的动物总称，与它的拉丁语名称来源及相关研究词相邻。

entries.definition: a rural god with goat legs in Roman myth
entries.definitionCN: 罗马神话中半羊半人的乡野神

entries.definition: relating to the animals of a region
relating to the study of regional animals
the plants of a region, taken as a group
wild animals living in a natural setting
the scientific study of animals

normalIntro.en: Fauna pairs with flora: fauna for animals, flora for plants, both from Latin names.
normalIntro.cn: fauna 与 flora 成对：fauna 指动物，flora 指植物，二者都来自拉丁语名称。

normal.en: Fauna is named after a Roman goddess of the countryside.
normal.cn: fauna 得名于罗马乡野女神。

normal.en: Linnaeus used Fauna Suecica as a book title for Swedish animals.
normal.cn: 林奈用《Fauna Suecica》作瑞典动物志的书名。

normal.en: The adjective faunal describes anything about regional animals.
normal.cn: 形容词 faunal 描述与地区动物有关的事物。

normal.en: Marine fauna means all the animals of the sea.
normal.cn: marine fauna 指海洋中的全部动物。

normal.en: Compare flora: flora is plants, fauna is animals.
normal.cn: 对比 flora：flora 是植物，fauna 是动物。

abstract.en: Picture a rainforest at night, every call coming from a different animal.
abstract.cn: 想象夜晚的雨林，每一声叫都来自不同的动物。

abstract.en: Imagine two columns in a museum, one of plants and one of animals.
abstract.cn: 想象博物馆里的两列展品，一列植物，一列动物。

abstract.en: Think of a thick catalogue listing every animal of an island.
abstract.cn: 想象一本厚名录，列出一座岛上的每一种动物。

examples.en: The local fauna includes several rare bats.
examples.cn: 本地动物群包括几种稀有的蝙蝠。

examples.en: Divers came to study the marine fauna of the reef.
examples.cn: 潜水者前来研究礁石的海洋动物群。

examples.en: The guide lists the fauna and flora of the park.
examples.cn: 这本指南列出了公园的动物与植物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fauna」听起来像「放哪」——动物太多，不知放哪；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 Fauna（乡野女神，Faunus 的姐妹或配偶）→ 林奈《Fauna Suecica》用作动物志书名 → 英语 fauna，核心义「一片土地上的动物全体」。

sensesIntro.en: Fauna begins as the name of a goddess and a book title, then settles into the collective animals of a region, animal life at large, and a catalogue of animals.
sensesIntro.cn: fauna 从女神名与书名开始，逐渐固定为某地动物全体、泛指动物生命，以及动物名录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: every animal of one place listed in a single column.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一地方的所有动物被列在同一列。

branches.en: Regional animals are the collective sense.
branches.cn: 地区动物全体是集合义项。

branches.en: Animal life at large is the broad sense.
branches.cn: 泛指动物生命是广义义项。

branches.en: A catalogue of animals is the book sense.
branches.cn: 动物名录是书名义项。

branches.en: A regional fauna is one visible part of animal life as a whole.
branches.cn: 地区动物群是整体动物生命的一个可见部分。

branches.en: A fauna in print records the animal life of a place.
branches.cn: 成书的动物志记录一个地方的动物生命。

intro.en: Fauna is a Latin name turned scientific term; its English family includes faunal and faunistic.
intro.cn: fauna 是由拉丁语名称转为科学术语的词，其英语词族包括 faunal 与 faunistic。

latinIntro.en: Latin Fauna names a rural goddess, and Faunus names the related god of woods and fields.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 Fauna 是乡野女神之名，Faunus 是相关的树林与田野之神。

items.example: Fauna is the goddess behind the term.
items.exampleCN: Fauna 是该术语背后的女神。

items.example: Faunus is the male counterpart of Fauna.
items.exampleCN: Faunus 是 Fauna 的男性对应神。

items.example: Fauna is now a scientific collective noun.
items.exampleCN: fauna 现在是科学上的集合名词。

items.example: Faunal surveys count the animals of a site.
items.exampleCN: faunal 调查统计一个地点的动物。

items.example: Faunistic research maps where animals live.
items.exampleCN: faunistic 研究绘制动物的分布。

items.example: A faunist records the animals of a district.
items.exampleCN: faunist 记录一个地区的动物。

items.meaning: the study of regional animal life
items.example: Faunistics compares animal lists from many places.
items.exampleCN: faunistics 比较许多地方的动物名录。

items.meaning: a goddess of flowers, later plant life
items.example: Flora is the plant counterpart of Fauna.
items.exampleCN: flora 是 fauna 的植物对应词。

items.example: The suffix -al forms faunal.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 faunal。

definition_zh: 传真；传真机；传真文件；用传真发送
definition_en: a copy of a document sent over a telephone line, or the machine or system that sends it; also to send a document this way
core_image: 一张纸顺着电话线滑过去，在另一端的机器里重新吐出来
scene: 办公室角落里的旧机器吱吱响着，吐出客户刚签好的合同。The old machine in the corner printed a fax of the signed contract.
sceneCN: 这里 fax 是「传真文件」（第 1 个义项：通过电话线传送的文件副本）；句意：角落里的旧机器打印出一份签好合同的传真。

derivatives.zh: 远程传真；电话网传真（tele- 与 fax 组合，强调远距离传送）
传真回传服务（fax 与 back 组合，按请求把存档文件传真回去）

senses.title: A document sent by fax
senses.definition: a copy of a document transmitted over a telephone line
senses.definitionCN: 通过电话线传送的文件副本
senses.example: She sent the invoice by fax.
senses.exampleCN: 她把发票传真了过去。
senses.why: Facsimile first meant an exact copy, so the fax is that copy sent down a wire.
senses.whyCN: facsimile 最初指精确副本，fax 则是顺着线路送出去的那份副本。

senses.title: The machine itself
senses.definition: the device that scans a page and sends or receives the copy
senses.definitionCN: 扫描纸页并收发副本的机器
senses.example: Our fax machine is out of paper again.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的传真机又没纸了。
senses.why: The device takes the name of the copy it handles, a common metonymy.
senses.whyCN: 机器直接借用了它所处理的副本之名，这是常见的转喻。

senses.title: The telephone service
senses.definition: the system or service that carries documents over telephone lines
senses.definitionCN: 通过电话线传送文件的系统或业务
senses.example: The clinic keeps a fax line for overseas results.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所保留一条传真线路，用来接收海外结果。
senses.why: Once the copy became routine, the word named the whole channel as well.
senses.whyCN: 当副本传送变成日常业务后，这个词也用来指整条通道。

senses.title: To send by fax
senses.definition: to send a document to someone using a fax machine
senses.definitionCN: 用传真机把文件发送给某人
senses.example: Please fax the signed form to our London office.
senses.exampleCN: 请把签好的表格传真到我们伦敦的办公室。
senses.why: English turns the noun into a verb without adding a suffix, so the act takes the name of the thing.
senses.whyCN: 英语不加后缀就把名词直接用作动词，于是动作也用了这件东西的名字。

intro.en: Fax is a twentieth-century clipping of facsimile, which comes from the Latin phrase fac simile, meaning make a similar thing.
intro.cn: fax 是二十世纪对 facsimile 的截短；facsimile 出自拉丁语短语「fac simile」，意为「做出相似的东西」。

items.en: Facere means to make, and similis means like or similar.
items.cn: facere 意为制造，similis 意为相像、相似。

items.en: The phrase fac simile, make a similar thing, is the direct source of facsimile.
items.cn: 短语「fac simile」意为「做出相似的东西」，是 facsimile 的直接来源。

items.en: Facsimile names an exact copy of a book, map, or manuscript.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语中，facsimile 指书籍、地图或手稿的精确副本。

items.en: Fax is clipped from facsimile in telegraph and telephone traffic.
items.cn: 二十世纪的电报与电话通信把 facsimile 截短成 fax。

items.en: The office fax machine makes the short word a household term.
items.cn: 办公室传真机让这个短词进入千家万户。

items.en: Email and digital scans replace much fax traffic, but fax number and by fax remain in use.
items.cn: 电子邮件与数字扫描取代了大量传真业务，但「fax number」与「by fax」仍在使用。

note.en: Fax is the clipped descendant of facsimile, and its nearest neighbours are the old telegraph systems and the digital tools that replaced it.
note.cn: fax 是 facsimile 截短后的后代，它最近的邻居既有古老的电报系统，也有取代它的数字工具。

entries.definition: an exact copy of a document or picture
entries.definitionCN: 精确副本；传真机的旧称（fax 的完整形式）

entries.definition: a fax sent over a public telephone network
entries.definitionCN: 通过公共电话网传送的传真

entries.definition: a service that sends stored documents to a caller by fax
entries.definitionCN: 按来电请求把存档文件传真回去的服务

entries.definition: an older system for sending printed messages over telegraph lines
entries.definitionCN: 电传；旧式电报打印系统

entries.definition: a message sent from one computer to another
a digital image made from a paper document
entries.definitionCN: 扫描件；由纸质文件制成的数字图像

normalIntro.en: Fax is a short, practical word: it names the copy, the machine, the channel, and the act of sending.
normalIntro.cn: fax 是个简短而实用的词：它同时指副本、机器、通道和发送动作。

normal.en: Fax is a clipping of facsimile, so the long word and the short word mean the same copy.
normal.cn: fax 是 facsimile 的截短形式，长词与短词指的是同一份副本。

normal.en: Send a fax and the page arrives as a copy at the other end.
normal.cn: 发一份传真，纸页就以副本的形式到达另一端。

normal.en: A fax machine scans the page, dials the number, and prints the copy.
normal.cn: 传真机扫描纸页、拨号，然后打印出副本。

normal.en: By fax means through that telephone channel rather than by post.
normal.cn: 「by fax」指通过那条电话通道，而不是通过邮寄。

normal.en: Fax works as a verb too: you fax a form to someone.
normal.cn: fax 也可以作动词：你把表格传真给某人。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of paper sliding along a telephone wire.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸沿着电话线滑行。

abstract.en: Imagine one machine swallowing a page while another prints it far away.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器吞下纸页，另一台在远处把它打印出来。

abstract.en: Think of a photocopy that travels instead of staying on the desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一份复印件不是留在桌上，而是出门旅行。

examples.en: She sent the invoice by fax.
examples.cn: 她把发票传真了过去。

examples.en: Our fax machine is out of paper again.
examples.cn: 我们的传真机又没纸了。

examples.en: Please fax the map to the hotel before noon.
examples.cn: 请在中午前把地图传真给酒店。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「法克斯」——法克斯把一页纸塞进电话线，另一头立刻吐出同样的纸；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 facere（做）+ similis（相似）→「fac simile」（做出相似的东西）→ 英语 facsimile（精确副本）→ 二十世纪截短为 fax，核心义「复制并传送同一份文件」。

sensesIntro.en: Fax moves from the document copy to the machine, then to the telephone service, and finally to the verb of sending.
sensesIntro.cn: fax 从文件副本走到机器，再走到电话业务，最后变成「用传真发送」的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet of paper sliding down a wire and reappearing on a distant desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张纸顺着线路滑走，在远处的桌上重新出现。

branches.en: The document copy is the founding sense.
branches.cn: 文件副本是最初的义项。

branches.en: The machine is named after the copy it handles.
branches.cn: 机器因处理副本而得名。

branches.en: The channel sense grows from routine office use.
branches.cn: 通道义项从日常办公使用中长出来。

branches.en: The verb turns the whole process into an action.
branches.cn: 动词把整个过程变成一个动作。

branches.en: A copy and the machine that makes it are two sides of one act.
branches.cn: 副本与制造副本的机器是同一个动作的两面。

intro.en: Fax looks like a modern clipping, but its family reaches back to the Latin phrase fac simile: facsimile, telefax, faxback, faxed, and faxing all circle the same copy.
intro.cn: fax 看似现代截短词，但它的词族可追到拉丁语短语「fac simile」：facsimile、telefax、faxback、faxed 与 faxing 都围绕同一份副本。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere, to make, and similis, similar, combine in fac simile, literally make a similar thing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facere（制造）与 similis（相似）组合成「fac simile」，字面意思是「做出相似的东西」。

items.example: Facere supplies the making in fac simile.
items.exampleCN: facere 为「fac simile」提供「制造」这一层意思。

items.example: Similis supplies the likeness in fac simile.
items.exampleCN: similis 为「fac simile」提供「相似」这一层意思。

items.example: The phrase fac simile became English facsimile.
items.exampleCN: 短语「fac simile」演变为英语 facsimile。

items.meaning: an exact copy of a document
items.example: Facsimile is the full word behind fax.
items.exampleCN: facsimile 是 fax 背后的完整词形。

items.example: Fax shortens the long word in everyday use.
items.exampleCN: fax 在日常使用中把长词缩短。

items.meaning: to send a document by fax
items.example: Please fax the page today.
items.exampleCN: 请今天把这一页传真过来。

items.meaningCN: 复数或第三人称单数词尾
items.example: The suffix -es forms faxes.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -es 构成 faxes。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms faxed.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 faxed。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms faxing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 faxing。

items.example: The prefix tele- forms telefax.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 tele- 构成 telefax。

items.meaning: a fax sent over a telephone network
items.example: Telefax adds distance to fax.
items.exampleCN: telefax 给 fax 加上「远距离」的意思。

definition_zh: 无畏的；不怕的；大胆的；毫无惧色的
definition_en: not afraid of danger, criticism, or difficulty; showing no fear
core_image: 一个人走进漆黑的山洞，脚步没有一丝停顿
scene: 深夜的火警响起，消防员逆着人群冲进燃烧的大楼。The firefighters entered the burning building, fearless and focused.
sceneCN: 这里 fearless 是「无所畏惧的」（第 1 个义项：面对危险毫不害怕）；句意：消防员冲进燃烧的大楼，毫无惧色，全神贯注。

derivatives.zh: 无畏地；毫不害怕地（fearless 加 -ly 构成副词）
无畏；无所畏惧（fearless 加 -ness 构成名词）

senses.title: Not afraid of danger
senses.definition: showing no fear when facing physical harm or a dangerous situation
senses.definitionCN: 面对人身伤害或危险处境时毫不害怕
senses.example: The fearless diver went back into the flooded cave.
senses.exampleCN: 那名无畏的潜水员再次进入被水淹没的洞穴。
senses.why: Fearless is fear plus -less, so the adjective simply removes the emotion named by fear.
senses.whyCN: fearless 由 fear 加 -less 构成，后缀直接去掉了 fear 所指的那种情绪。

senses.title: Bold before power
senses.definition: willing to speak or act without fearing criticism, authority, or disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 敢于发声或行动，不怕批评、权威或他人的不满
senses.example: A fearless young reporter questioned the minister.
senses.exampleCN: 一位无所畏惧的年轻记者质问部长。
senses.why: The absence of fear moves from bodily danger to social pressure, where the risk is disapproval rather than injury.
senses.whyCN: 「没有恐惧」从人身危险移到社会压力：这里的风险不是受伤，而是被否定。

senses.title: Utterly without fear
senses.definition: having no fear at all, especially in a look, manner, or temperament
senses.definitionCN: 完全没有恐惧，尤指神情、举止或性情
senses.example: She gave a fearless smile as the verdict was read.
senses.exampleCN: 宣读裁决时，她露出毫无惧色的微笑。
senses.why: Because -less is absolute, the word can describe a total absence rather than a moment of courage.
senses.whyCN: 因为 -less 表示完全缺乏，这个词可以描写彻底的「没有」，而不只是一时的勇敢。

senses.title: Bold in style or performance
senses.definition: done with bold confidence, especially in art, sport, or performance
senses.definitionCN: 以大胆自信的方式完成，尤指艺术、运动或表演
senses.example: The band gave a fearless performance that split the critics.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队的演出大胆放肆，让评论家分成两派。
senses.why: A visible absence of hesitation becomes a label for work that takes risks without apology.
senses.whyCN: 看得见的「不犹豫」变成一种标签，用来形容毫不怯场、敢于冒险的作品。

intro.en: Fearless joins Old English fǣr, sudden danger, with -lēas, free from; the modern sense of fear as an emotion developed later, and the exact deeper root of the danger word is uncertain.
intro.cn: fearless 由古英语 fǣr（突降的灾祸、危险）与 -lēas（没有、免于）结合而成；fear 后来才转指内心的害怕，这个「危险」词更早的词根并无定论。

items.en: A root such as *per-, to try or risk, is often proposed for the danger word, but the reconstruction is not settled.
items.cn: 有人为这个表示危险的词提出 *per-（尝试、冒险）之类的词根，但重构结果并无定论。

items.en: *fēr- or *feraz names sudden danger or ambush in the Germanic languages.
items.cn: *fēr- 或 *feraz 在日耳曼语族中指突降的危险或伏击。

items.en: Fǣr means a sudden calamity, attack, or danger, not the inner feeling of dread.
items.cn: fǣr 指突降的灾祸、袭击或危险，而不是内心恐惧的感觉。

items.en: -lēas means free from or without and forms adjectives of absence.
items.cn: -lēas 意为「没有、免于」，用来构成表示「缺乏」的形容词。

items.en: Fearless appears as a description of people and animals that show no fear.
items.cn: 中古英语里，fearless 用来描写不露惧色的人与动物。

items.en: As fear became mainly the inner emotion, fearless widened to criticism, crowds, and bold style.
items.cn: 当 fear 主要转指内心情绪后，fearless 便扩展到批评、人群与大胆风格。

note.en: Fearless keeps one of the oldest English suffixes, and its meaning sits between the emotion word fear and the wider field of courage words.
note.cn: fearless 保留了英语最古老的后缀之一，意义落在情绪词 fear 与更广的「勇气」义场之间。

entries.definition: the emotion of being afraid
feeling afraid or showing fear
the quality of being fearless
ready to face danger or pain
entries.definitionCN: 勇敢的；愿意面对危险或痛苦的

entries.definition: confident and willing to take risks
fearless and adventurous
entries.definitionCN: 无畏而敢于冒险的（正式用语）

normalIntro.en: Fearless is built inside English from fear and the Old English suffix -less, and the whole family turns around that missing emotion.
normalIntro.cn: fearless 是英语内部用 fear 与古英语后缀 -less 构成的，整个词族都围绕「缺失的那种情绪」打转。

normal.en: Fearless is fear plus the suffix -less, which means without.
normal.cn: fearless 是 fear 加上后缀 -less，后者意为「没有」。

normal.en: The suffix -less is absolute, so fearless means no fear at all, not merely a little courage.
normal.cn: 后缀 -less 表示彻底缺乏，所以 fearless 是「完全没有恐惧」，而不只是一点勇气。

normal.en: Fearlessness is the noun, and fearlessly is the adverb.
normal.cn: fearlessness 是名词，fearlessly 是副词。

normal.en: Fearless often describes people who face danger, criticism, or a crowd.
normal.cn: fearless 常用来描写面对危险、批评或人群的人。

normal.en: Compare brave: brave stresses action despite fear, while fearless stresses the absence of fear.
normal.cn: 对比 brave：brave 强调尽管害怕仍然行动，fearless 强调恐惧本身的缺席。

abstract.en: Picture a child walking past a growling dog without slowing down.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子走过一条低吼的狗，脚步一点没有放慢。

abstract.en: Imagine standing before a full hall and speaking without a tremor.
abstract.cn: 想象站在满座大厅前讲话，声音没有一丝颤抖。

abstract.en: Think of a lamp that burns steadily in a dark, windy cave.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯在黑暗多风的洞穴里稳稳燃烧。

examples.en: The fearless climber kept going through the storm.
examples.cn: 那名无畏的登山者顶着风暴继续前行。

examples.en: She is fearless when she speaks her mind in a meeting.
examples.cn: 她在会上直言不讳时毫无惧色。

examples.en: A fearless reporter exposed the scandal.
examples.cn: 一位无所畏惧的记者揭露了这桩丑闻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「菲儿勒斯」——菲儿勒斯走在漆黑的巷子里，脚步一点也不乱；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 fǣr（突降的灾祸、危险）+ -lēas（没有、免于）→ fearless「没有恐惧」；fear 后来才转指内心的害怕。

sensesIntro.en: Fearless begins with physical courage, moves to courage before people and power, then to a total absence of fear, and finally to bold style.
sensesIntro.cn: fearless 从面对人身危险的勇气，走到面对他人与权力的勇气，再到彻底的「没有恐惧」，最后指大胆的风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person walking straight into a dark cave without slowing down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人径直走进漆黑的山洞，脚步没有丝毫放慢。

branches.en: Courage in physical danger is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 在人身危险中的勇气是基本义项。

branches.en: Courage before power moves the risk into society.
branches.cn: 面对权力的勇气把风险移到社会层面。

branches.en: The absolute suffix yields the sense of no fear at all.
branches.cn: 绝对化的后缀带来「完全没有恐惧」的义项。

branches.en: A fearless manner becomes a label for bold work.
branches.cn: 无所畏惧的姿态变成大胆作品的标签。

branches.en: Both a flooded cave and a packed hall test the same absence of hesitation.
branches.cn: 被淹的洞穴与满座的礼堂，考验的是同一种「不犹豫」。

intro.en: Fearless is built inside English from fear and the Old English suffix -less; its family includes fearlessly, fearlessness, fearful, and fearsome.
intro.cn: fearless 是英语内部由 fear 与古英语后缀 -less 构成的；它的词族包括 fearlessly、fearlessness、fearful 与 fearsome。

latinIntro.en: Fearless has no Latin ancestry: fear is a Germanic word, and -less comes from Old English -lēas, so the Latin column stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: fearless 没有拉丁语渊源：fear 是日耳曼语词，-less 来自古英语 -lēas，所以拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.exampleCN: fear 最初指危险，而不是内心情绪。

items.example: The verb fear names the emotion directly.
items.exampleCN: 动词 fear 直接指这种情绪。

items.example: The suffix -less builds adjectives of absence.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -less 构成表示「缺乏」的形容词。

items.example: Fearless joins fear with the suffix -less.
items.exampleCN: fearless 把 fear 与后缀 -less 结合起来。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms fearlessly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 fearlessly。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms fearlessness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 fearlessness。

items.example: Fearful uses the suffix -ful instead.
items.exampleCN: fearful 改用后缀 -ful。

items.example: Fearsome uses the suffix -some.
items.exampleCN: fearsome 使用后缀 -some。

items.example: The suffix -ful builds fearful.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ful 构成 fearful。

items.example: The suffix -some builds fearsome.

definition_zh: 多产的；肥沃的；繁殖力强的；创造力旺盛的
definition_en: producing abundant offspring, crops, or ideas; fertile and productive
core_image: 一棵树的枝条上同时挂满果实、花朵和种子
scene: 雨季过后，河边的果树上结满了果子，种子随风落进湿土。After the rains, the fecund orchard produced more fruit than the family could pick.
sceneCN: 这里 fecund 是「多产的；丰饶的」（第 1 个义项：能大量结果或繁殖）；句意：雨后，丰产的果园结出的果子多得一家人摘不完。

pos.zh: 多产的；肥沃的；创造力旺盛的

derivatives.zh: 多产；肥沃；创造力（fecund 加 -ity 构成名词）
使受孕；使肥沃（fecund 加 -ate 构成动词）
不育的；不毛的（in- 加 fecund 构成否定形容词）

senses.title: Producing many offspring
senses.definition: able to produce many offspring, seeds, or young
senses.definitionCN: 能产生大量后代、种子或幼体的
senses.example: The fecund weed spread across the field in one season.
senses.exampleCN: 这种繁殖力强的野草在一个季节里就铺满了田地。
senses.why: Latin fecundus means fruitful, so the first sense is sheer reproductive abundance.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fecundus 意为「结果实的」，所以第一个义项就是纯粹的繁殖丰盛。

senses.title: Fertile land
senses.definition: of soil or land, producing abundant crops or vegetation
senses.definitionCN: 指土壤或土地能产出大量作物或植被
senses.example: The fecund soil of the delta feeds three villages.
senses.exampleCN: 三角洲肥沃的土壤养活了三个村庄。
senses.why: The same fruitfulness is transferred to the ground that yields the crops.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「结果实」的能力被转移到长出作物的土地上。

senses.title: Creative and productive
senses.definition: producing many ideas, works, or inventions
senses.definitionCN: 产生大量想法、作品或发明的
senses.example: Her fecund imagination filled three notebooks in a month.
senses.exampleCN: 她旺盛的想象力一个月就写满了三个笔记本。
senses.why: Mental output borrows the image of a plant that keeps bearing fruit.
senses.whyCN: 精神产出借用了植物不断结果实的意象。

senses.title: Abounding in something
senses.definition: full of or rich in a particular quality, especially in the phrase fecund in
senses.definitionCN: 富于某种特质，尤用于「fecund in」这一搭配
senses.example: The era was fecund in new theories of government.
senses.exampleCN: 那个时代富于关于政府的新理论。
senses.why: The prepositional use generalizes fruitfulness into abundance of any kind.
senses.whyCN: 带介词的用法把「结果实」泛化为任何形式的丰富。

intro.en: Fecund comes straight from Latin fecundus, fruitful or fertile. The deeper root is uncertain; it is often linked to a root for suckling, also seen in femina and fetus, but that connection is debated.
intro.cn: fecund 直接来自拉丁语 fecundus（多产的、肥沃的）；更早的词根来源存疑，常被联系到表示「吮吸、哺育」的词根（也见于 femina 与 fetus），但这层联系仍有争议。

items.en: Fecundus means fruitful, fertile, or productive.
items.cn: fecundus 意为结果实的、肥沃的、多产的。

items.en: Fecundare means to make fruitful, and fecunditas means fruitfulness.
items.cn: fecundare 意为使结果实，fecunditas 意为丰产、肥沃。

items.en: Some scholars connect fecundus with a suckling root shared by femina and fetus; the link is not certain.
items.cn: 一些学者把 fecundus 与 femina、fetus 共有的「哺育」词根联系起来，但这一联系并不确定。

items.en: French fécond develops in parallel and later reinforces the English word.
items.cn: 法语 fécond 平行发展，后来又强化了英语中的这个词。

items.en: Fecund enters English as a learned word for fertile land, plants, and animals.
items.cn: 十六世纪，fecund 作为书面词进入英语，指肥沃的土地、植物与动物。

items.en: The word widens from fields and animals to minds that keep producing ideas.
items.cn: 这个词从田地与动物扩展到不断产生想法的头脑。

note.en: Fecund belongs to a Latin family of fertility words, and its nearest everyday neighbours are fertile, prolific, and fruitful.
note.cn: fecund 属于拉丁语系的「丰产」词族，日常最接近的邻居是 fertile、prolific 与 fruitful。

entries.definition: the state of being fecund
to make fertile or fruitful
not fertile or productive
able to produce young, crops, or ideas
entries.definitionCN: 能生育的；肥沃的；能产生想法的

entries.definition: producing many offspring, works, or results
producing good results or abundant growth

normalIntro.en: Fecund is a learned Latin adjective, and its whole family describes abundance: fecundity, fecundate, and the rare negative infecund.
normalIntro.cn: fecund 是个书面化的拉丁语形容词，它的整个词族都在描述「丰盛」：fecundity、fecundate，以及少见的否定形式 infecund。

normal.en: Fecund is a Latin loanword; its noun is fecundity.
normal.cn: fecund 是拉丁语借词，它的名词形式是 fecundity。

normal.en: Fecund soil yields several crops in one year.
normal.cn: 肥沃的土壤一年能长出好几茬作物。

normal.en: A fecund imagination keeps producing new ideas.
normal.cn: 旺盛的想象力不断产生新想法。

normal.en: Fecundate is the rare verb that means make fruitful.
normal.cn: fecundate 是少见的动词，意为「使结果实」。

normal.en: Fertile, prolific, and fecund overlap, but fecund sounds bookish and Latin.
normal.cn: fertile、prolific 与 fecund 意义重叠，但 fecund 更书面、更有拉丁味。

abstract.en: Picture a tree whose branches are heavy with fruit and seed.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵树，枝条被果实和种子压得低垂。

abstract.en: Imagine a pod bursting and seeds raining onto wet soil.
abstract.cn: 想象一只豆荚爆开，种子像雨点落进湿土。

abstract.en: Think of a writer filling one notebook after another without a pause.
abstract.cn: 想象一位作家一本接一本地写满笔记，中间没有停顿。

examples.en: The fecund river valley supports three harvests a year.
examples.cn: 这片丰产的河谷一年能支撑三季收成。

examples.en: Her fecund imagination gave the novel dozens of subplots.
examples.cn: 她旺盛的想象力给这部小说添了几十条支线。

examples.en: Rabbits are famously fecund and multiply within months.
examples.cn: 兔子以繁殖力强著称，几个月内就能成倍增加。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「菲昆德」——菲昆德家的果园年年结满果子，送都送不完；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 fecundus（多产的、肥沃的）→ 英语 fecund，核心义「能不断结出果实」；更早词根存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Fecund starts with biological abundance, moves to rich soil, then to creative output, and finally to any kind of abundance.
sensesIntro.cn: fecund 从生物的繁殖丰盛，走到肥沃的土壤，再到创造性产出，最后泛指任何形式的丰富。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tree whose branches carry fruit, flowers, and seed at the same time.
core.cn: 核心意象：一棵树的枝条同时挂着果实、花朵和种子。

branches.en: Reproductive abundance is the original sense.
branches.cn: 繁殖上的丰盛是最初的义项。

branches.en: Rich soil is fruitfulness moved to the land.
branches.cn: 肥沃的土壤是把「结果实」移到土地上。

branches.en: Creative output is fruitfulness moved to the mind.
branches.cn: 创造性产出是把「结果实」移到头脑里。

branches.en: The phrase fecund in widens the word to any abundance.
branches.cn: 「fecund in」这一搭配把词义扩展到任何形式的丰富。

branches.en: Seed and soil are two halves of the same harvest image.
branches.cn: 种子与土壤是同一幅丰收图景的两半。

intro.en: Fecund is a Latin adjective, and English builds a small learned family around it: fecundity, fecundate, and the negative infecund.
intro.cn: fecund 是拉丁语形容词，英语围绕它构成一个小型书面词族：fecundity、fecundate 与否定形式 infecund。

latinIntro.en: Latin fecundus means fruitful, fecunditas means fruitfulness, and fecundare means to make fruitful.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fecundus 意为结果实的，fecunditas 意为丰产，fecundare 意为使结果实。

items.example: Fecundus is the direct source of fecund.
items.exampleCN: fecundus 是 fecund 的直接来源。

items.example: Fecunditas supplies the noun fecundity.
items.exampleCN: fecunditas 提供名词 fecundity 的词干。

items.example: Fecundare leads to the English verb fecundate.
items.exampleCN: fecundare 引出英语动词 fecundate。

items.example: Fecund keeps the Latin meaning intact.
items.exampleCN: fecund 完整保留了拉丁语含义。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms fecundity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 fecundity。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms fecundate.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ate 构成 fecundate。

items.example: The prefix in- negates fecund.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 否定 fecund。

items.example: The prefix in- forms infecund.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 构成 infecund。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms fecundity.

items.example: The suffix -ate forms fecundate.

definition_zh: 联邦；联合会；联盟；联合；结盟
definition_en: a union of states or organizations under a central authority, or the act of forming such a union
core_image: 许多小旗子围着一张圆桌插成一圈，桌上摊着同一份契约
scene: 几个独立的州把各自的旗帜并排挂进同一座大厅，共用一套法律和一支军队。The federation brought twelve separate states under one central parliament.
sceneCN: 这里 federation 是「联邦」（第 1 个义项：由多个州或地区组成的统一国家）；句意：这个联邦把十二个独立的州置于同一个中央议会之下。

pos.zh: 联邦；联合会；联盟；联合（的行为）

derivatives.zh: 联邦的；联邦制的（federation 去掉 -ion 后的形容词形式）
使结成联邦；联合（federation 的动词形式）
联邦主义；联邦制（federal 加 -ism 构成名词）
邦联；同盟（con- 加 federation，指较松散的联合）

senses.title: A federal state
senses.definition: a state formed by several regions or states that keep some internal powers under a central government
senses.definitionCN: 由若干地区或州组成、各自保留部分内部权力并共有一个中央政府的国家
senses.example: Canada is a federation of ten provinces and three territories.
senses.exampleCN: 加拿大是由十个省和三个地区组成的联邦。
senses.why: Latin foedus means treaty, so separate units are bound together by one agreement.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 foedus 意为条约，所以各个单位是被同一份契约绑在一起的。

senses.title: An association of organizations
senses.definition: an umbrella organization made up of clubs, unions, or societies
senses.definitionCN: 由俱乐部、工会或协会组成的伞状组织
senses.example: The national federation of chess clubs meets every second year.
senses.exampleCN: 全国象棋俱乐部联合会每两年开一次会。
senses.why: The treaty image shrinks from states to voluntary bodies that agree to act together.
senses.whyCN: 契约意象从国家缩小到自愿结社的团体，它们同意共同行动。

senses.title: An alliance of groups
senses.definition: a union of separate groups acting together for a shared purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为共同目的而一起行动的独立团体的联合
senses.example: A loose federation of charities shared one warehouse.
senses.exampleCN: 一个松散的慈善联盟共用一座仓库。
senses.why: The political bond loosens into any joint arrangement among independent groups.
senses.whyCN: 政治上的结合松弛下来，泛指独立团体之间的任何联合安排。

senses.title: The act of forming a union
senses.definition: the process or act of joining separate units into one union
senses.definitionCN: 把独立单位联合成一个整体的过程或行为
senses.example: The federation of the two leagues took ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个联盟的合并花了十年。
senses.why: The noun of action keeps the verb federate visible behind the finished union.
senses.whyCN: 表示动作的名词让「结盟」这个动词在已完成的联合背后仍然可见。

intro.en: Federation comes from Latin foedus, a treaty or league, through the verb foederare and the Late Latin noun foederatio.
intro.cn: federation 来自拉丁语 foedus（条约、盟约），经动词 foederare 与晚期拉丁语名词 foederatio 进入英语。

items.en: Foedus, genitive foederis, means a treaty, league, or covenant.
items.cn: foedus（属格 foederis）意为条约、联盟或盟约。

items.en: Foedus is generally related to fides, faith or trust, so a league rests on a pledged word.
items.cn: foedus 一般认为与 fides（信义、信任）同源，所以联盟建立在彼此许下的诺言上。

items.en: Foederare means to bind by treaty, and foederatio names the union that results.
items.cn: foederare 意为以条约结合，foederatio 指由此形成的联合。

items.en: Fédération and fédérer carry the political sense through French.
items.cn: fédération 与 fédérer 把这一政治含义带进法语。

items.en: Federation enters English political writing during the debates over the American union.
items.cn: 十八世纪，federation 在关于美国联合的辩论中进入英语政治写作。

items.en: The word extends to federations of labour unions, sports clubs, and industry bodies.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到工会、体育俱乐部与行业机构的联合会。

note.en: Federation keeps a Latin family of treaty words, and its meaning sits between a tight federal state and a loose alliance.
note.cn: federation 保留了一个拉丁语「契约」词族，意义介于紧密的联邦国家与松散的联盟之间。

entries.definition: relating to a federation or its central government
entries.definitionCN: 联邦的；与联邦中央政府有关的

entries.definition: to join separate units into a federation
a system in which power is shared between central and regional governments
a looser union of states or groups
the act or state of being joined together
a formal agreement to work together

normalIntro.en: Federation is a treaty word: Latin foedus binds the units, and English builds federal, federate, federalism, and confederation from it.
normalIntro.cn: federation 是个「契约」词：拉丁语 foedus 把各单位绑在一起，英语又由它构成 federal、federate、federalism 与 confederation。

normal.en: Federation comes from Latin foedus, a treaty or covenant.
normal.cn: federation 来自拉丁语 foedus，意为条约或盟约。

normal.en: Federal is the adjective and federate is the verb.
normal.cn: federal 是形容词，federate 是动词。

normal.en: A federation of states keeps one central government.
normal.cn: 由各州组成的联邦只有一个中央政府。

normal.en: A sports federation is an umbrella body of clubs.
normal.cn: 体育联合会是各个俱乐部的伞状组织。

normal.en: A confederation is looser than a federation.
normal.cn: 邦联比联邦更松散。

abstract.en: Picture many small flags planted around one round table.
abstract.cn: 想象许多小旗子插在同一张圆桌周围。

abstract.en: Imagine separate towns signing one shared contract.
abstract.cn: 想象几个分开的城镇签下同一份契约。

abstract.en: Think of many clubs sending one delegate to a single hall.
abstract.cn: 想象许多俱乐部各派一名代表走进同一座大厅。

examples.en: Canada is a federation of ten provinces and three territories.
examples.cn: 加拿大是由十个省和三个地区组成的联邦。

examples.en: The international football federation sets the rules for the game.
examples.cn: 国际足球联合会制定这项运动的规则。

examples.en: A loose federation of local clubs shared one meeting hall.
examples.cn: 一个松散的本地俱乐部联盟共用一座会议厅。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「菲德瑞申」——菲德瑞申把许多小旗收进同一只箱子，大家签同一份契约；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 foedus（属格 foederis，条约、盟约）→ 晚期拉丁语 foederatio（结盟）→ 英语 federation，核心义「以契约结成一体」。

sensesIntro.en: Federation moves from a full federal state to an association of organizations, then to a looser alliance, and finally to the act of joining.
sensesIntro.cn: federation 从完整的联邦国家，走到组织联合会，再到更松散的联盟，最后指「联合」这一行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many small flags planted around one round table with a single contract on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多小旗子插在同一张圆桌周围，桌上摊着一份契约。

branches.en: A federal state is the full political sense.
branches.cn: 联邦国家是完整的政治义项。

branches.en: An association of organizations shrinks the treaty to clubs.
branches.cn: 组织联合会把契约缩小到俱乐部层面。

branches.en: A loose alliance keeps only the shared purpose.
branches.cn: 松散联盟只保留共同目的。

branches.en: The act sense names the joining itself.
branches.cn: 动作义项直接指「联合」这件事。

branches.en: A federal state and a loose alliance differ in how tightly the contract binds.
branches.cn: 联邦国家与松散联盟的差别，在于契约绑得有多紧。

intro.en: Federation comes from Latin foedus, a treaty, and English builds federal, federate, federalism, and confederation around the same bond.
intro.cn: federation 来自拉丁语 foedus（条约），英语围绕同一种「绑定」构成 federal、federate、federalism 与 confederation。

latinIntro.en: Latin foedus, genitive foederis, means treaty or league; foederare means to bind by treaty, and foederatio names the resulting union.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 foedus（属格 foederis）意为条约或联盟；foederare 意为以条约结合，foederatio 指由此形成的联合。

items.exampleCN: 词干 foeder- 出现在 foederatio 中。

items.example: Foederare leads to the English verb federate.
items.exampleCN: foederare 引出英语动词 federate。

items.example: Foederatio is the direct model for federation.
items.exampleCN: foederatio 是 federation 的直接范本。
