definition_zh: 虚弱的；无力的；微弱的；软弱无能的
definition_en: lacking physical strength, force, or effectiveness
core_image: 一根被风吹弯的细树枝，抬不起头
scene: 病房里，老人抬手都费劲，说话只剩气声。The nurse noted how feeble the patient had become after the long illness.
sceneCN: 这里 feeble 是「虚弱的」（第 1 个义项：身体虚弱无力）；句意：护士注意到这位病人在久病之后变得多么虚弱。

derivatives.zh: 由 feeble 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「虚弱地；无力地」
由 feeble 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「虚弱；无力」
由前缀 en-（使）加 feeble 构成，义为「使虚弱；使衰弱」
由 enfeeble 加 -ment 构成，义为「衰弱的状态」

senses.title: Physically weak
senses.definition: lacking bodily strength, especially because of age or illness
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏体力，尤指因年老或患病而虚弱
senses.example: The old horse was too feeble to pull the cart.
senses.exampleCN: 那匹老马太虚弱了，拉不动车。
senses.why: The Latin source meant lamentable or pitiable, and pity for a helpless body produced the modern sense of physical weakness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为「值得哀哭的、可怜的」，人们对无助身体的怜悯，催生了今天「身体虚弱」的义项。

senses.title: Lacking force as an argument
senses.definition: of an argument, excuse, or reason: not convincing or forceful
senses.definitionCN: 指论证、借口或理由不能令人信服、没有力度
senses.example: His feeble excuse convinced nobody.
senses.exampleCN: 他那站不住脚的借口谁也没骗过。
senses.why: A body too weak to stand suggests a claim too weak to stand, so the image moves from limbs to reasoning.
senses.whyCN: 站不住的身体，自然让人想到站不住的论断，意象便从四肢移到说理。

senses.title: Faint in sound or light
senses.definition: of sound or light: very faint and barely perceptible
senses.definitionCN: 指声音或光线非常微弱，几乎难以察觉
senses.example: A feeble glow came from the dying lamp.
senses.exampleCN: 将熄的灯发出微弱的光。
senses.why: The bent twig barely holds itself up, and any signal that can hardly carry itself is described the same way.
senses.whyCN: 弯下的细枝几乎撑不住自己，任何难以传达出去的信号也用同一个词形容。

senses.title: Lacking power or authority
senses.definition: of a person, government, or institution: unable to act effectively
senses.definitionCN: 指个人、政府或机构无法有效行动
senses.example: The feeble response of the council let the problem grow.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会软弱无力的回应让问题越滚越大。
senses.why: Strength of the body becomes strength of office, so a body that cannot resist becomes an authority that cannot act.
senses.whyCN: 身体的力气延伸到职位的权力，因此无法抵抗的身体就变成无法行动的权威。

senses.title: Low in intensity or amount
senses.definition: small in intensity, amount, or effect
senses.definitionCN: 强度、数量或效果都很小
senses.example: The company made a feeble effort to cut waste.
senses.exampleCN: 公司为减少浪费做出的努力微乎其微。
senses.why: Effort behaves like a muscle: too little of it moves nothing, so the word measures any weak force.
senses.whyCN: 努力像肌肉一样，太少就推不动任何东西，于是这个词也用来衡量任何微弱的力量。

senses.title: Dim in memory or perception
senses.definition: of a memory or impression: dim and uncertain
senses.definitionCN: 指记忆或印象模糊、不确定
senses.example: Only a feeble memory of the song remained.
senses.exampleCN: 那首歌只留下一点模糊的记忆。
senses.why: What is faint in light is faint in the mind, so a weak flame supplies the image for a weak recollection.
senses.whyCN: 在光线上显得微弱的，在头脑里也同样微弱，于是将熄的火苗成了模糊回忆的意象。

senses.title: Weak in character
senses.definition: of a person: easily led or lacking moral firmness
senses.definitionCN: 指人容易被左右、缺乏坚定的品格
senses.example: He was too feeble to refuse their demand.
senses.exampleCN: 他太软弱，不敢拒绝他们的要求。
senses.why: A body that cannot resist pressure suggests a will that cannot resist pressure either.
senses.whyCN: 承受不住压力的身体，暗示同样承受不住压力的意志。

senses.title: Hard to detect, as a pulse
senses.definition: of a pulse: weak and difficult to detect
senses.definitionCN: 指脉搏微弱、难以摸到
senses.example: The doctor recorded a feeble pulse and called for help.
senses.exampleCN: 医生摸到微弱的脉搏，立刻叫人来帮忙。
senses.why: The bodily sense narrows to a clinical sign, where a weak beat is the clearest evidence of low vitality.
senses.whyCN: 身体义项收窄成一个临床征象：微弱的心跳正是生命力低落最清楚的证据。

intro.en: Feeble comes from Latin flebilis, lamentable, from flere, to weep, through Old French feble.
intro.cn: feeble 来自拉丁语 flebilis（值得哀哭的、可怜的），源于 flere（哭泣），经古法语 feble 进入英语。

items.en: Flere means to weep, and flebilis means that which is to be wept over.
items.cn: flere 意为哭泣，flebilis 意为「值得为之哭泣的」。

items.en: Flebilis also means lamentable or pitiable, the emotional seed of the later sense.
items.cn: flebilis 也指可悲的、可怜的，这是后来词义的情感种子。

items.en: Feble carries the word into French, where it already means weak.
items.cn: feble 把词带入法语，在法语里已经表示虚弱。

items.en: Feble is recorded in English by the thirteenth century, already meaning weak.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪前后记录下 feble，意为虚弱。

items.en: Modern English fixes the spelling as feeble and extends it to arguments, sounds, and institutions.
items.cn: 现代英语把拼写固定为 feeble，并把它扩展到论证、声音与机构。

note.en: Feeble belongs to a small family of weakness words and has a look-alike in foible, which comes from the same French source.
note.cn: feeble 属于一小族表示「虚弱」的词，而形近的 foible 其实同出法语来源。

entries.definition: in a weak or ineffective way
entries.definitionCN: 虚弱地；无力地，由 feeble 加 -ly 构成

entries.definition: the state of being weak
entries.definitionCN: 虚弱的状态，由 feeble 加 -ness 构成

entries.definition: a small weakness of character
entries.definitionCN: 性格上的小缺点，与 feeble 同出古法语 feble，并非只是拼写相近

entries.definition: lacking strength or power
entries.definitionCN: 虚弱的；力量不足的，是最中性的说法

entries.definition: delicate and easily broken, especially of an old person
entries.definitionCN: 形容老人身体纤弱、容易受伤

entries.definition: weak in body, especially from age
entries.definitionCN: 因年迈而体弱，语体偏正式、偏医学

normalIntro.en: Feeble is a weeping word that turned into a weakness word, and its family is built with plain English suffixes.
normalIntro.cn: feeble 本是一个「哭泣」的词，后来变成「虚弱」的词，它的词族由朴素的英语后缀构成。

normal.en: The Latin source flebilis meant lamentable, so pity and weakness were linked from the start.
normal.cn: 拉丁语来源 flebilis 意为「值得哀哭的」，因此怜悯与虚弱从一开始就绑在一起。

normal.en: Feeble most often describes an old or ill body, as in a feeble old man.
normal.cn: feeble 最常形容年老或患病的身体，如「a feeble old man」。

normal.en: A feeble excuse or argument is one that cannot stand up to pressure.
normal.cn: 「feeble excuse」或「feeble argument」指经不起推敲的借口或论证。

normal.en: The adverb is feebly and the noun is feebleness, both regular suffixations.
normal.cn: 副词是 feebly，名词是 feebleness，都是规则的后缀派生。

normal.en: Compare frail and weak: feeble stresses a lack of force that invites pity.
normal.cn: 对比 frail 与 weak：feeble 强调的是一种引人怜悯的无力。

abstract.en: Picture a thin branch bending under its own weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细枝被自己的重量压弯。

abstract.en: Imagine a paper shield that crumples at the first blow.
abstract.cn: 想象一面纸做的盾牌，第一下就被打皱。

abstract.en: Think of a lamp whose flame has almost gone out.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯，火苗几乎已经熄灭。

examples.en: The illness left him feeble for months.
examples.cn: 这场病让他虚弱了好几个月。

examples.en: She gave a feeble excuse and left the room.
examples.cn: 她给了一个站不住脚的借口就离开了房间。

examples.en: A feeble light flickered in the corridor.
examples.cn: 走廊里闪着微弱的光。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「feeble」读近「非薄」——又非又薄，自然虚弱；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 flere（哭泣）→ flebilis（值得哀哭的、可怜的）→ 古法语 feble → 英语 feeble；核心义由「可怜」转为「软弱无力」。

sensesIntro.en: Feeble starts from a weak body, then lends that weakness to arguments, light, authority, effort, memory, character, and finally to a pulse.
sensesIntro.cn: feeble 从虚弱的身体出发，再把这种无力借给论证、光线、权威、努力、记忆、性格，最后落到脉搏上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin branch that bends under its own weight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根被自身重量压弯的细枝。

branches.en: A weak body and a weak pulse are the same bodily evidence seen at two scales.
branches.cn: 虚弱的身体与微弱的脉搏，是同一身体证据在两个尺度上的表现。

branches.en: A claim that cannot stand is a weak body in argument form.
branches.cn: 站不住的论断，就是论证形态下的虚弱身体。

branches.en: Faint sound and faint light inherit the image of a barely held flame.
branches.cn: 微弱的声音与光线继承了「几乎撑不住的火苗」这一意象。

branches.en: Powerless institutions and weak wills both fail to resist pressure.
branches.cn: 无力的机构与软弱的意志，同样抵挡不住压力。

branches.en: Small effort and dim memory are both measured as low intensity.
branches.cn: 微小的努力与模糊的记忆，都被衡量为低强度。

intro.en: Feeble is built from a Latin root for weeping plus a Latin suffix, and English adds -ly, -ness, and en- around it.
intro.cn: feeble 由表示「哭泣」的拉丁词根加拉丁后缀构成，英语又围绕它加上 -ly、-ness 与 en-。

latinIntro.en: Latin flere means to weep, flebilis means lamentable, and Old French feble passes the word to English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 flere 意为哭泣，flebilis 意为可怜的，古法语 feble 把词传给英语。

items.example: Flere supplies the weeping root of the family.
items.exampleCN: flere 提供这一词族「哭泣」的词根。

items.example: The suffix -bilis turns a verb into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -bilis 把动词变成形容词。

items.example: Flebilis is the direct Latin ancestor of feeble.
items.exampleCN: flebilis 是 feeble 的直接拉丁语祖先。

items.example: Feble is the Old French form that English borrowed.
items.exampleCN: feble 是英语借入的古法语形式。

items.example: Feeble is the modern English adjective.
items.exampleCN: feeble 是现代英语形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the adverb feebly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成副词 feebly。

items.example: Feebly describes an action done without strength.
items.exampleCN: feebly 描述没有力气地做某事。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms the noun feebleness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成名词 feebleness。

items.example: Feebleness names the condition itself.
items.exampleCN: feebleness 指虚弱这一状态本身。

items.example: The prefix en- forms the verb enfeeble.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 en- 构成动词 enfeeble。

definition_zh: 假装；编造；伪造
definition_en: to pretend to have a feeling or condition, or to invent something false
core_image: 一张临时戴上的面具，把真实的脸藏在后面
scene: 他明明没事，却捂着肚子皱眉，让同事以为他病了。He feigned a stomach ache to leave the meeting early.
sceneCN: 这里 feign 是「假装」（第 1 个义项：装出某种感受或状况）；句意：他假装肚子疼，好提前离开会议。

derivatives.zh: 由 feign 加 -ed 构成，义为「假装的；装出来的」
由 feign 加 -ing 构成，义为「假装的行为」
由否定前缀 un- 加 feigned 构成，义为「真诚的；不做作的」
与 feign 同出古法语 feindre，义为「佯攻；假动作」，但拼写与读音已经分化

senses.title: To pretend to have a feeling
senses.definition: to pretend that you have a particular feeling, illness, or condition
senses.definitionCN: 假装自己具有某种感受、疾病或状况
senses.example: She feigned surprise when she heard the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到那个消息时，她假装很吃惊。
senses.why: Latin fingere means to shape or mould, so feigning is shaping a false surface that others will read as real.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fingere 意为塑造、捏造，所以假装就是塑出一层假的外表，让别人当成真的。

senses.title: To invent a false story
senses.definition: to invent an excuse, reason, or story that is not true
senses.definitionCN: 编造不真实的借口、理由或故事
senses.example: He feigned an urgent call and slipped away.
senses.exampleCN: 他编了个紧急电话的借口，溜走了。
senses.why: Shaping clay became shaping words, so a made-up story is a thing manufactured rather than found.
senses.whyCN: 捏土变成捏词，编出来的故事因此是被制造出来的，而不是被发现的。

senses.title: To hide true feelings behind a show
senses.definition: to conceal what one really feels by showing a false outward sign
senses.definitionCN: 用虚假的外在表现掩盖真实感受
senses.example: They feigned indifference to the criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对那些批评装作无所谓。
senses.why: A mask covers a face, so the word names not only the false show but the act of covering.
senses.whyCN: 面具遮住脸，因此这个词不仅指假的表现，也指遮盖这个动作本身。

senses.title: To counterfeit something
senses.definition: to make a false copy of something, such as a signature or a document
senses.definitionCN: 伪造签名、文件等物品的假副本
senses.example: The dealer feigned an old signature on the canvas.
senses.exampleCN: 那个商人在画布上伪造了一个旧签名。
senses.why: The shaping root also produced fiction and figment, so false objects made by hand belong to the same family.
senses.whyCN: 「塑造」词根也生出 fiction 与 figment，因此手工造出的假物件同样属于这一族。

senses.title: To pretend not to know
senses.definition: to pretend ignorance or innocence, often to avoid blame
senses.definitionCN: 装作不知道或无辜，常为了逃避责任
senses.example: The clerk feigned ignorance of the missing files.
senses.exampleCN: 那名职员对丢失的文件装作不知情。
senses.why: Ignorance can be worn like a mask, and the wearer hopes no one looks behind it.
senses.whyCN: 无知可以像面具一样戴上，戴的人只希望没人绕到面具后面看。

senses.title: Of sleep or death: pretended
senses.titleCN: 假装的（睡眠、死亡等状态）
senses.definition: used of states such as sleep or death that are pretended rather than real
senses.definitionCN: 用于睡眠、死亡等被装出来而非真实的状态
senses.example: The soldier feigned death until the patrol passed.
senses.exampleCN: 那名士兵装死，直到巡逻队走过去。
senses.why: The most complete mask is a whole bodily state, so the word reaches sleep, swoons, and death.
senses.whyCN: 最彻底的面具是一整个身体状态，于是这个词延伸到睡眠、昏厥与死亡。

senses.title: To make a false move in war
senses.definition: in military use, to make a false show of an action in order to deceive
senses.definitionCN: 军事用语，做出虚假的行动姿态以迷惑对方
senses.example: The troop feigned a retreat to draw the enemy forward.
senses.exampleCN: 那支部队佯装撤退，把敌人引向前方。
senses.why: Deception in the field is the oldest use of a false appearance, where a pretended move wins real ground.
senses.whyCN: 战场上的欺骗是「假外观」最古老的用法：佯装的一步能换来真实的阵地。

senses.title: To invent in poetry or art
senses.definition: in older literary use, to invent or imagine something in speech, poetry, or art
senses.definitionCN: 较古老的文学用法，指在言谈、诗歌或艺术中虚构、想象
senses.example: The poet feigned a world where no winter came.
senses.exampleCN: 那位诗人虚构了一个没有冬天的世界。
senses.why: The Latin verb also meant to devise, so poets feigned worlds long before anyone feigned a signature.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本来也有「构想」之义，所以诗人虚构世界，远早于有人伪造签名。

intro.en: Feign comes from Latin fingere, to shape or devise, through Old French feindre.
intro.cn: feign 来自拉丁语 fingere（塑造、构想），经古法语 feindre 进入英语。

items.en: Fingere means to shape, mould, or devise with the hands or the mind.
items.cn: fingere 意为用手或心去塑造、捏制、构想。

items.en: Fictio, a shaping or a feigning, grows from the same verb and gives English fiction.
items.cn: fictio 意为塑造或虚构，同出这一动词，并给出英语 fiction。

items.en: Feindre carries the shaping sense into French as to pretend or dissemble.
items.cn: feindre 把「塑造」之义带入法语，意为假装、掩饰。

items.en: Feign enters English in the early fourteenth century with the sense to disguise or pretend.
items.cn: feign 在十四世纪前后进入英语，意为掩饰或假装。

items.en: Modern English keeps the pretence sense and revives the older literary sense of inventing.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「假装」义，并让「虚构」这一较古老的文学义继续存在。

note.en: Feign shares its shaping root with fiction and figment, and it is easily confused with the shorter feint.
note.cn: feign 与 fiction、figment 共享「塑造」词根，又很容易和更短的 feint 混淆。

entries.definition: a deceptive move, especially in sport or war
entries.definitionCN: 佯攻；假动作；与 feign 同出古法语 feindre，只是拼写与读音分化，并非两个无关的词

entries.definition: an invented story or untrue account
entries.definitionCN: 虚构作品；同出拉丁语 fingere（塑造）

entries.definition: something invented in the mind
entries.definitionCN: 凭空想象之物；同出拉丁语 fingere

entries.definition: to act as if something is true when it is not
entries.definitionCN: 假装，是最日常、最中性的说法

entries.definition: to imitate the appearance of something
entries.definitionCN: 模拟；做出与某物相似的外观，偏技术语体

entries.definition: to hide true feelings or intentions
entries.definitionCN: 掩饰真实感情或意图，语体正式

normalIntro.en: Feign is a shaping word: the pretence is manufactured, and its relatives are fiction, figment, and the look-alike feint.
normalIntro.cn: feign 是一个「塑造」的词：假象是被造出来的，它的亲属有 fiction、figment，以及形近的 feint。

normal.en: Fingere, to shape, is the source, so feign is to shape a false front.
normal.cn: fingere 意为塑造，是词源所在，所以 feign 就是塑出一个假门面。

normal.en: Keep the pair apart: feign is pretence, feint is a deceptive move.
normal.cn: 把这一对分清：feign 是假装，feint 是假动作。

normal.en: Feign illness, feign surprise, and feign ignorance are the commonest pairs.
normal.cn: 「feign illness」「feign surprise」「feign ignorance」是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Fiction and figment share the same shaping root, which helps fix the spelling.
normal.cn: fiction 与 figment 共享「塑造」词根，能帮忙记住拼写。

normal.en: Compare pretend: feign is more formal and suggests a deliberate mask.
normal.cn: 对比 pretend：feign 更正式，也更有「刻意戴面具」的意味。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pulling a mask down over a face.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把面具拉下来盖住脸。

abstract.en: Imagine clay shaped into a fruit that is not fruit.
abstract.cn: 想象把黏土捏成一个不是水果的水果。

abstract.en: Think of a curtain drawn across a window at noon.
abstract.cn: 想象正午时有人把窗帘拉上。

examples.en: He feigned illness to avoid the exam.
examples.cn: 他装病逃避考试。

examples.en: She feigned interest in the lecture.
examples.cn: 她对那场讲座假装感兴趣。

examples.en: Feigning calm, the pilot reported the fault.
examples.cn: 飞行员假装镇定，报告了故障。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「feign」读近「非真」——不是真的，就是假装；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 fingere（塑造、捏造）→ 拉丁语 fictio（塑造、虚构）→ 古法语 feindre（假装）→ 英语 feign，核心义「造出一个能骗过人的假外壳」。

sensesIntro.en: Feign moves from pretending a feeling, to inventing a story, to concealing, counterfeiting, feigning ignorance, sleep, a military move, and finally a poem.
sensesIntro.cn: feign 从装出某种感受，走到编造故事、掩饰情感、伪造物件、装作不知、装睡装死、佯动，最后走到诗里的虚构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mask pulled over a real face.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张拉下来盖住真脸的面具。

branches.en: A pretended feeling and an invented story are both shaped surfaces.
branches.cn: 装出的感受与编出的故事，都是塑出来的表面。

branches.en: Concealment is the mask seen from behind.
branches.cn: 掩饰是从面具背后看这件事。

branches.en: A counterfeit object is a mask given to a thing instead of a face.
branches.cn: 伪造的物件，是给物品而不是脸戴上的面具。

branches.en: Feigned ignorance and a feigned retreat both win by making others misread.
branches.cn: 装作不知与佯装撤退，都靠让别人误读而取胜。

branches.en: A pretended death is the fullest mask, and a feigned world is the largest one.
branches.cn: 装死是最彻底的面具，虚构的世界则是最大的那一张。

intro.en: Feign comes from a Latin shaping verb whose family includes fiction, figment, and the French feint.
intro.cn: feign 来自拉丁语表示「塑造」的动词，其词族包括 fiction、figment 与法语的 feint。

latinIntro.en: Latin fingere means to shape or devise, and fictio names the shaping or the thing shaped.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fingere 意为塑造、构想，fictio 指塑造这件事或被塑造之物。

items.example: Fingere supplies the shaping image behind feign.
items.exampleCN: fingere 提供 feign 背后「塑造」的意象。

items.example: Fictio leads to the English fiction.
items.exampleCN: fictio 引出英语的 fiction。

items.example: Feindre is the French bridge to English.
items.exampleCN: feindre 是通往英语的法语桥梁。

items.example: Feign keeps the pretence sense in English.
items.exampleCN: feign 在英语中保留「假装」义。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms the adjective feigned.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成形容词 feigned。

items.example: Feigned describes a feeling that is not real.
items.exampleCN: feigned 描述并不真实的感受。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms the noun feigning.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成名词 feigning。

items.example: Fiction descends from the same Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: fiction 同出这一拉丁动词。

items.example: Figment keeps the inventing sense of the root.
items.exampleCN: figment 保留词根「构想」之义。

definition_zh: 女权主义；女性主义
definition_en: the belief that women should have equal rights and opportunities, and the movement that works for them
core_image: 一群女性合力推开同一扇长期紧闭的门
scene: 会议室里，几位女性提出同工同酬的要求，并追问由谁来定规则。Feminism gave them a shared language for that demand.
sceneCN: 这里 feminism 是「女权主义」（第 1 个义项：主张女性应享有平等权利的思想）；句意：女权主义给了她们表达这一要求的共同语言。

derivatives.zh: 由 feminism 换后缀 -ist 构成，义为「女权主义者」
由 feminist 加 -ic 构成，义为「带有女权主义色彩的」
由前缀 anti-（反对）加 feminism 构成，义为「反女权主义」
由前缀 pro-（支持）加 feminist 构成，义为「支持女权主义的」

senses.title: The belief in equal rights for women
senses.definition: the belief that women should have the same rights and opportunities as men
senses.definitionCN: 认为女性应与男性享有同等权利与机会的信念
senses.example: Feminism begins with the simple claim that women are people with rights of their own.
senses.exampleCN: 女权主义始于这样一个主张：女性是拥有完整权利的人。
senses.why: Latin femina means woman and the suffix -ism names a doctrine, so the word first names a belief about women.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 femina 意为女人，后缀 -ism 表示一种主张，因此这个词首先指一套关于女性的信念。

senses.title: The organised movement
senses.definition: the organised movement that works for the rights and status of women
senses.definitionCN: 为女性权利与地位而行动的有组织运动
senses.example: Feminism changed the law on equal pay within a single generation.
senses.exampleCN: 女权运动在一代人的时间里改变了同工同酬的法律。
senses.why: A belief held by many people and acted on in public becomes a movement, and the same noun covers both.
senses.whyCN: 一套被许多人持有并在公共领域付诸行动的信念会成为运动，同一个名词便同时覆盖两者。

senses.title: The academic field
senses.definition: the body of scholarship that studies gender, power, and the situation of women
senses.definitionCN: 研究性别、权力与女性处境的学术体系
senses.example: Feminism entered the university as a field with its own questions and methods.
senses.exampleCN: 女权主义作为一门有自身问题与方法的学科进入了大学。
senses.why: A movement that keeps asking why turns its questions into a discipline, so the doctrine becomes a field of study.
senses.whyCN: 一个不断追问「为什么」的运动把追问变成学科，于是主张变成了研究领域。

senses.title: Awareness of gendered power
senses.definition: an awareness of how gender shapes power in everyday life
senses.definitionCN: 对性别如何在日常生活中塑造权力的敏感
senses.example: Her feminism showed in the questions she asked at the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 她的性别权力意识体现在面试时提出的问题上。
senses.why: The doctrine sharpens into a way of noticing, so feminism can name an everyday attentiveness rather than a programme.
senses.whyCN: 这套主张会磨成一种觉察方式，因此 feminism 也能指日常的敏感，而不只是纲领。

senses.title: A strand or wave of the movement
senses.titleCN: （某一流派或浪潮的）女权主义
senses.definition: one branch or wave of the movement, such as liberal or radical feminism
senses.definitionCN: 运动中的某一分支或浪潮，如自由派或激进派女权主义
senses.example: Liberal feminism works through law and reform rather than revolution.
senses.exampleCN: 自由派女权主义通过法律与改革而非革命来推进。
senses.why: A broad movement divides into named currents, and each current keeps the umbrella word for itself.
senses.whyCN: 一个宽泛的运动分成有名字的支流，每一支都把这把大伞的名字留给自己用。

senses.title: Advocacy within one profession
senses.definition: advocacy for women inside a particular field, such as medicine or law
senses.definitionCN: 在医学、法律等某一具体领域内为女性发声的主张
senses.example: Feminism in medicine asks who was left out of the trials.
senses.exampleCN: 医学领域的女性主张会追问谁被排除在试验之外。
senses.why: The suffix -ism can attach to any field, so the same imbalance produces a feminism of that field.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ism 可以接到任何领域上，因此同一种失衡会在该领域里长出一种「主义」。

senses.title: The outlook it forms in a person
senses.definition: the set of attitudes and habits that the movement has produced in a person
senses.definitionCN: 运动在一个人身上养成的态度与习惯
senses.example: His feminism was visible in how he shared the housework.
senses.exampleCN: 他的女权意识体现在他如何分担家务上。
senses.why: A public doctrine settles into private habit, and the noun follows it into the home.
senses.whyCN: 公共的主张会沉淀为私人的习惯，这个词也跟着走进家里。

senses.title: The legacy of the movement
senses.definition: the historical legacy of the movement and the changes it left behind
senses.definitionCN: 运动留下的历史遗产与它带来的改变
senses.example: Feminism left its mark on the wording of the constitution.
senses.exampleCN: 女权主义在宪法的措辞上留下了印记。
senses.why: A movement that wins changes leaves a legacy, and later generations name that legacy with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 赢得改变的运动留下遗产，后来的人仍用同一个词来命名这份遗产。

intro.en: Feminism joins Latin femina, woman, with the suffix -ism, and reaches English from French in the 1890s.
intro.cn: feminism 由拉丁语 femina（女人）加后缀 -ism 构成，十九世纪九十年代经法语进入英语。

items.en: Femina means woman, and femininus means of or belonging to a woman.
items.cn: femina 意为女人，femininus 意为女性的、属于女人的。

items.en: The ending -ismus names a practice or a doctrine, and it becomes English -ism.
items.cn: 词尾 -ismus 表示某种实践或主张，后来变成英语的 -ism。

items.en: Feminisme appears in French in the nineteenth century, with more than one claimant for its first use.
items.cn: féminisme 于十九世纪出现在法语中，首用者不止一种说法。

items.en: Feminism enters English in the 1890s as the name of a cause and a body of writing.
items.cn: feminism 在十九世纪九十年代进入英语，指一项事业和一批写作。

items.en: Modern English expands the word into waves, academic fields, and named currents.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词扩展到浪潮、学术领域与有名目的支流。

note.en: Feminism sits at the centre of a family built on Latin femina, and its nearest neighbours are the person, the adjective, and rival labels.
note.cn: feminism 位于以拉丁语 femina 为核心的词族中央，最近的邻居是表示人的词、形容词以及竞争性的标签。

entries.definition: a supporter of equal rights for women
entries.definitionCN: 女权主义者；由 feminism 换后缀 -ist 构成

entries.definition: having qualities associated with women
entries.definitionCN: 女性化的；同出拉丁语 femina

entries.definition: soft or womanish, said of a man and often as an insult
entries.definitionCN: 女子气的（用于男性，常含贬义）；同出拉丁语 ex 加 femina

entries.definition: a movement centring the experience of Black women
entries.definitionCN: 以黑人女性经验为中心的主张，与女权主义部分重叠

entries.definition: the campaign for the right of women to vote
entries.definitionCN: 争取女性投票权的运动，范围比女权主义窄

entries.definition: hatred of or prejudice against women
entries.definitionCN: 对女性的憎恶或偏见，正好与女权主义相对

normalIntro.en: Feminism is femina plus -ism, and its family splits neatly between the belief, the person, and the adjective.
normalIntro.cn: feminism 就是 femina 加 -ism，它的词族清楚地分成主张、人与形容词三块。

normal.en: Femina is Latin for woman, and -ism names a doctrine, so the word says a doctrine about women.
normal.cn: femina 是拉丁语「女人」，-ism 表示主张，合起来就是一套关于女性的主张。

normal.en: Feminism and feminist differ by one suffix: -ism is the belief, -ist is the person.
normal.cn: feminism 与 feminist 只差一个后缀：-ism 是主张，-ist 是人。

normal.en: Liberal feminism, radical feminism, and second wave feminism are common labels.
normal.cn: 「liberal feminism」「radical feminism」「second wave feminism」是常见标签。

normal.en: The word is first recorded in English in the 1890s, borrowed from French.
normal.cn: 这个词最早在十九世纪九十年代见于英语，借自法语。

normal.en: Compare womanism, a term coined to centre the experience of Black women.
normal.cn: 对比 womanism，这个词是为以黑人女性经验为中心而造的。

abstract.en: Picture a row of women pushing the same heavy door.
abstract.cn: 想象一排女性一起推同一扇沉重的门。

abstract.en: Imagine a march where thousands hold one slogan.
abstract.cn: 想象一场游行，几千人举着同一句口号。

abstract.en: Think of a seminar room where a new question is written on the board.
abstract.cn: 想象一间研讨室，黑板上写着一个新问题。

examples.en: Feminism argues that equal pay is a right and not a favour.
examples.cn: 女权主义主张同工同酬是权利而不是恩惠。

examples.en: Feminism has changed the language of law and work.
examples.cn: 女权主义改变了法律与工作的语言。

examples.en: She studies feminism alongside political theory.
examples.cn: 她把女权主义与政治理论放在一起研究。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fem」读近「粉」，可联想粉色与女性，再加 -ism（主义），记作「女性主义」；这只是读音联想，词源上 fem 来自拉丁语 femina。

root: 拉丁语 femina（女人）→ 拉丁语 femininus（女性的）→ 法语 féminisme（十九世纪）→ 英语 feminism，核心义「以女性为中心的主张与运动」。

sensesIntro.en: Feminism starts as a belief, becomes a movement, a scholarship, an awareness, a current, a field-specific cause, a personal outlook, and finally a legacy.
sensesIntro.cn: feminism 先是一套信念，再成为运动、学问、觉察、支流、某一领域的主张、个人态度，最后成为一份遗产。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many hands pushing one long-closed door.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多只手一起推开一扇久闭的门。

branches.en: The plain doctrine is the root sense of the whole family.
branches.cn: 最朴素的信念是整族词义的根。

branches.en: A doctrine acted on in public becomes a movement.
branches.cn: 在公共领域付诸行动的主张成为运动。

branches.en: Study and legacy are what a long movement leaves behind.
branches.cn: 学问与遗产，是一场长久运动留下的东西。

branches.en: Awareness in public life and habit at home are the same outlook at two scales.
branches.cn: 公共生活里的觉察与家中的习惯，是同一种眼光在两个尺度上。

branches.en: Named currents and field-specific causes are the doctrine divided by scope.
branches.cn: 有名目的支流与特定领域的主张，是按范围切开的同一套主张。

intro.en: Feminism is built from the Latin noun for woman plus the doctrine suffix -ism, and English adds -ist and -ic around it.
intro.cn: feminism 由拉丁语「女人」这一名词加表主张的后缀 -ism 构成，英语又围绕它加上 -ist 与 -ic。

latinIntro.en: Latin femina means woman, femininus means of a woman, and medieval Latin -ismus names a doctrine.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 femina 意为女人，femininus 意为女性的，中世纪拉丁语 -ismus 表示一种主张。

items.example: Femina is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: femina 是整族词的基底。

items.example: Femininus leads to the English feminine.
items.exampleCN: femininus 引出英语的 feminine。

items.meaningCN: 表示实践或主张的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ismus becomes English -ism.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ismus 变成英语的 -ism。

items.example: The suffix -ism forms feminism from the Latin base.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 在拉丁词基上构成 feminism。

items.example: Feminisme is the French form that English borrowed.
items.exampleCN: féminisme 是英语借入的法语形式。

items.example: Feminism keeps both the belief and the movement.
items.exampleCN: feminism 同时保留信念与运动两面。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms the noun feminist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 构成名词 feminist。

items.meaning: a supporter of equal rights for women
items.example: Feminist names the person behind the doctrine.
items.exampleCN: feminist 指主张背后的人。

items.example: Feminine keeps the descriptive sense of the root.
items.exampleCN: feminine 保留词根的描述义。

definition_zh: 女权主义者；女权主义的
definition_en: a person who supports the belief that women should have equal rights, or relating to that belief
core_image: 一个站在队伍前排、把牌子举过头顶的人
scene: 她在编辑部里坚持把女作者的书评排上头版，也坦然接受别人这样称呼她。The editor was a feminist long before the word became common in the newsroom.
sceneCN: 这里 feminist 是「女权主义者」（第 1 个义项：主张女性应享有平等权利的人）；句意：这位编辑早在该词流行于她的办公室之前，就已经是女权主义者了。

derivatives.zh: 把 -ist 换成 -ism 构成，义为「女权主义」，指主张本身
由 feminist 加 -ic 构成，义为「带有女权主义色彩的」
由前缀 anti-（反对）加 feminist 构成，义为「反女权主义者」
由前缀 pro-（支持）加 feminist 构成，义为「支持女权主义的」

senses.title: A supporter of equal rights for women
senses.definition: a person who believes that women should have equal rights and who works for them
senses.definitionCN: 相信女性应享有平等权利并为此行动的人
senses.example: Every feminist in the room signed the petition.
senses.exampleCN: 屋里每一位女权主义者都在请愿书上签了名。
senses.why: Latin femina means woman and the suffix -ist names a person who follows something, so the word first names the holder of the belief.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 femina 意为女人，后缀 -ist 表示追随某事的人，因此这个词首先指持有该信念的人。

senses.title: A participant in the movement
senses.definition: a person who takes part in the organised movement for the rights of women
senses.definitionCN: 参加为女性权利而组织起来的运动的人
senses.example: The feminists marched through the city before the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 投票之前，女权运动成员游行穿过城市。
senses.why: When many holders of a belief act together, the person named by -ist also becomes a member of a movement.
senses.whyCN: 当许多持有同一信念的人一起行动，-ist 所命名的人也就成了运动的成员。

senses.title: Relating to feminism
senses.definition: of ideas, writing, or action: connected with feminism
senses.definitionCN: 指思想、写作或行动与女权主义相关
senses.example: She wrote a feminist reading of the tax code.
senses.exampleCN: 她写了一篇对税制的女权主义解读。
senses.why: The same suffix also forms adjectives of adherence, so the word describes an outlook as well as a person.
senses.whyCN: 同一个后缀也能构成表示归属的形容词，因此这个词既指人也描述一种立场。

senses.title: A scholar who studies gender
senses.definition: a scholar whose work applies feminist thought to a field of study
senses.definitionCN: 把女权思想应用到某一研究领域的学者
senses.example: The feminist in the history department rewrote the reading list.
senses.exampleCN: 历史系的那位女性主义学者重写了阅读书目。
senses.why: The person who holds the doctrine also builds the scholarship, so a researcher can carry the same label.
senses.whyCN: 持有这套主张的人也在建设这门学问，因此研究者同样可以带这个标签。

senses.title: A man who supports the cause
senses.definition: a man who supports the rights of women and identifies with the movement
senses.definitionCN: 支持女性权利并认同这场运动的男性
senses.example: He calls himself a feminist without hesitation.
senses.exampleCN: 他毫不犹豫地称自己为女权主义者。
senses.why: The suffix names adherence, not sex, so the label can be carried by anyone who holds the belief.
senses.whyCN: 这个后缀命名的是归属而非性别，因此任何持有该信念的人都能带上这个标签。

senses.title: A follower of one current
senses.titleCN: 某一流派的女权主义者
senses.definition: a person associated with a specific current of the movement, such as radical or liberal feminism
senses.definitionCN: 与运动中某一具体流派相关的人，如激进派或自由派
senses.example: The radical feminist argued for a complete rethink of the family.
senses.exampleCN: 那位激进派女权主义者主张彻底重新思考家庭。
senses.why: A broad label divides into named currents, and each current has its own feminists.
senses.whyCN: 一个宽泛的标签会分成有名目的支流，每一支都有自己的女权主义者。

senses.title: A label used in public argument
senses.titleCN: （公共争论中的）女权主义标签
senses.definition: the label as used in public argument, sometimes approvingly and sometimes as an accusation
senses.definitionCN: 公共争论中使用的标签，有时表示赞同，有时带指责意味
senses.example: The word feminist was thrown at her as an insult, and she kept it.
senses.exampleCN: 有人把女权主义者这个词当作侮辱扔向她，她照收不误。
senses.why: A name for a person becomes a badge that others may pin on someone, and the wearer may accept or refuse it.
senses.whyCN: 指人的名称会变成别人别在你身上的徽章，戴的人可以接受，也可以拒绝。

senses.title: Of a work shaped by feminist ideas
senses.titleCN: 受女权思想影响的（作品）
senses.definition: of a text, film, or artwork: shaped by feminist ideas
senses.definitionCN: 指文本、电影或艺术作品受女权思想塑造
senses.example: The film offers a feminist reading of an old myth.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影对一则古老神话给出了女权主义的解读。
senses.why: The adjective reaches works of art, where an idea takes visible form and can be read by others.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词延伸到艺术作品，思想在那里获得可见的形状，也能被别人读出来。

intro.en: Feminist pairs Latin femina, woman, with the person suffix -ist, and comes to English from French in the 1890s.
intro.cn: feminist 把拉丁语 femina（女人）与表人的后缀 -ist 结合，十九世纪九十年代经法语进入英语。

items.en: Femina means woman, and it is the base of feminine, feminism, and feminist alike.
items.cn: femina 意为女人，是 feminine、feminism 与 feminist 共同的词基。

items.en: The ending -istes names the person who does or follows something, and Latin borrows it as -ista.
items.cn: 词尾 -istes 指从事或追随某事的人，拉丁语把它借作 -ista。

items.en: Feministe appears in French in the nineteenth century, modelled on feminisme.
items.cn: féministe 于十九世纪出现在法语中，是照着 féminisme 造出来的。

items.en: Feminist enters English in the 1890s as the name of a supporter of the rights of women.
items.cn: feminist 在十九世纪九十年代进入英语，指女性权利的支持者。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for persons, for ideas, and for works of art.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词用于人、用于思想，也用于艺术作品。

note.en: Feminist is the person word of the femina family, next to feminism, feminine, and the older suffragist label.
note.cn: feminist 是 femina 词族里指人的那个词，旁边是 feminism、feminine，以及更早的 suffragist 标签。

entries.definition: the belief and movement for equal rights
entries.definitionCN: 女权主义；与 feminist 只差后缀 -ism 与 -ist

entries.definition: having qualities associated with women
entries.definitionCN: 女性化的；同出拉丁语 femina

entries.definition: the quality of being feminine
entries.definitionCN: 女性气质；同出拉丁语 femina

entries.definition: a campaigner for the right of women to vote
entries.definitionCN: 争取女性投票权的活动家，比 feminist 出现更早、范围更窄

entries.definition: a person who centres the experience of Black women
entries.definitionCN: 以黑人女性经验为中心的人，与 feminist 部分重叠

entries.definition: a person who believes in equal rights for all
entries.definitionCN: 主张人人平等的人，范围比 feminist 更宽

normalIntro.en: Feminist is femina plus the person suffix -ist, and it works as both a noun and an adjective.
normalIntro.cn: feminist 就是 femina 加表人的后缀 -ist，既是名词也是形容词。

normal.en: Femina is Latin for woman and -ist names a person, so feminist is a person defined by a stand on women.
normal.cn: femina 是拉丁语「女人」，-ist 指人，所以 feminist 是因对女性的立场而被命名的人。

normal.en: The word is both noun and adjective: a feminist writer, a feminist argument.
normal.cn: 这个词既是名词也是形容词：「a feminist writer」「a feminist argument」。

normal.en: Suffragist is the older word for a campaigner for the vote; feminist is broader.
normal.cn: suffragist 是更早的争投票权者，feminist 的范围更宽。

normal.en: The word came into English in the 1890s from French.
normal.cn: 这个词于十九世纪九十年代从法语进入英语。

normal.en: Many feminists use the label for men who support the cause as well as for women.
normal.cn: 许多女权主义者把这个标签也用在支持该事业的男性身上。

abstract.en: Picture a person holding a sign at the front of a crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在人群最前面举着牌子。

abstract.en: Imagine a long line of marchers turning a corner together.
abstract.cn: 想象一长队游行者一起转过街角。

abstract.en: Think of a pen writing the word equality on a page.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔在纸上写下「平等」这个词。

examples.en: She became a feminist while studying law.
examples.cn: 她在学法律时成为了一名女权主义者。

examples.en: The journal published a feminist analysis of the census.
examples.cn: 那份期刊发表了一篇对人口普查的女权主义分析。

examples.en: Feminists have argued for equal pay for decades.
examples.cn: 女权主义者为同工同酬已经争论了几十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fem」读近「粉」，-ist 表人，可联想「粉色阵营里的人」，即女权主义者；这只是读音联想，词源上 fem 来自拉丁语 femina（女人）。

root: 拉丁语 femina（女人）→ 拉丁语 femininus（女性的）→ 法语 féministe（十九世纪）→ 英语 feminist，核心义「以女性平等为立场的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Feminist names a believer, a marcher, an outlook, a scholar, a male supporter, a follower of one current, a public label, and finally the adjective for a work.
sensesIntro.cn: feminist 先指信念的持有者，再指游行者、一种立场、学者、男性支持者、某一支流的追随者、公共标签，最后指形容作品的形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person at the front of a crowd, holding a sign overhead.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群最前面的一个人，把牌子举过头顶。

branches.en: The single believer is the plain, dictionary core.
branches.cn: 单个持有信念的人，是最朴素的词典核心义。

branches.en: The movement member and the male supporter are the same adherence at different scales.
branches.cn: 运动成员与男性支持者，是同一种归属在不同尺度上。

branches.en: The adjective for ideas and the adjective for artworks are one outlook in two materials.
branches.cn: 形容思想的形容词与形容作品的形容词，是同一种立场落在两种材料上。

branches.en: The scholar turns adherence into a body of work.
branches.cn: 学者把归属变成一套研究成果。

branches.en: A named current and a public label are the word divided by camp and by argument.
branches.cn: 有名目的支流与公共标签，是按阵营与争论切开的同一个词。

intro.en: Feminist is the Latin noun for woman plus the person suffix -ist, with feminism and feminine beside it.
intro.cn: feminist 由拉丁语「女人」这一名词加表人的后缀 -ist 构成，旁边是 feminism 与 feminine。

latinIntro.en: Latin femina means woman, femininus means of a woman, and Greek -istes passed through Latin as -ista.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 femina 意为女人，femininus 意为女性的，希腊语 -istes 经拉丁语变成 -ista。

items.meaning: a person who practises or follows
items.example: The suffix -ist forms feminist from the Latin base.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 在拉丁词基上构成 feminist。

items.meaning: a supporter of equal rights for women
items.example: Feminist names the person who holds the belief.

items.example: Feministic describes a tone or a style.

items.exampleCN: feminism 指人背后的那套主张。

definition_zh: 发酵；发酵过程；发酵作用
definition_en: the process in which yeast or bacteria break down sugar and produce alcohol, acid, or gas
core_image: 密封罐里的糖水自己翻腾，气泡一串串往上冒
scene: 厨房角落的玻璃罐里，糖水在酵母作用下慢慢冒泡，盖子被气体顶得微微鼓起。The cook sealed the jar and let the fermentation run for a week.
sceneCN: 这里 fermentation 是「发酵过程」（第 1 个义项：微生物把糖分解成酒精或酸的过程）；句意：厨师封好罐子，让发酵进行一周。

pos.zh: 发酵；发酵过程；发酵作用

derivatives.zh: （使）发酵；由拉丁语 fermentare 进入英语的动词，兼作名词指酵素
发酵的；能引起发酵的，由 ferment 加后缀 -ative 构成
发酵罐；进行发酵的微生物，由 ferment 加后缀 -er 构成
发酵过的，由 ferment 加后缀 -ed 构成

senses.title: The microbial breakdown of sugar
senses.titleCN: 微生物分解糖的发酵过程
senses.definition: the process by which yeast, bacteria, or other microbes break down sugar and produce alcohol, acid, or gas
senses.definitionCN: 酵母、细菌等微生物分解糖并产生酒精、酸或气体的过程
senses.example: The fermentation of grape juice is what turns it into wine.
senses.exampleCN: 葡萄汁的发酵正是把它变成葡萄酒的那一步。
senses.why: The core image is a sealed jar in which invisible microbes slowly rebuild sugar into something else.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一只密封罐，看不见的微生物在里面把糖慢慢改造成别的东西，这正是发酵最根本的一层。

senses.title: The state of fermenting
senses.definition: the condition of undergoing fermentation, especially while the process is still running
senses.definitionCN: 正处于发酵之中的状态，尤指过程尚未结束时
senses.example: The beer is still in fermentation, so the lid must stay loose.
senses.exampleCN: 啤酒还在发酵，所以盖子必须留松。
senses.why: From the process the word extends to the ongoing state, as in the everyday phrase in fermentation.
senses.whyCN: 由「过程」引申为「正在进行的状态」，常见说法就是 in fermentation，罐子还在冒泡的那段时间被单独命名了。

senses.title: Alcoholic fermentation in brewing
senses.definition: the conversion of sugar into alcohol by yeast, as used in wine, beer, and spirits
senses.definitionCN: 酵母把糖转化为酒精的过程，用于葡萄酒、啤酒与烈酒
senses.example: Brewers watch the fermentation closely to control the strength of the beer.
senses.exampleCN: 酿酒师密切关注发酵，以控制啤酒的度数。
senses.why: Yeast turning sugar into alcohol is the most familiar version of the bubbling jar image.
senses.whyCN: 酵母把糖变成酒精，是「罐中冒泡」这幅画面最常见、也最容易被认出的版本。

senses.title: Lactic fermentation in food
senses.definition: the action of bacteria that turn sugar into lactic acid, giving sour flavours and preserving food
senses.definitionCN: 细菌把糖变成乳酸的作用，带来酸味并保存食物
senses.example: Cabbage turns sour through lactic fermentation in the making of kimchi.
senses.exampleCN: 制作泡菜时，白菜通过乳酸发酵变酸。
senses.why: The same jar picture serves sour foods, where acid instead of alcohol is what the microbes leave behind.
senses.whyCN: 同一幅罐中冒泡的画面也适用于酸味食品，只是微生物留下的产物由酒精换成了酸。

senses.title: Industrial fermentation
senses.definition: a controlled large-scale process in tanks that uses microbes to make medicines, fuels, or food ingredients
senses.definitionCN: 在发酵罐中大规模控制微生物，以生产药物、燃料或食品原料的过程
senses.example: The plant uses industrial fermentation to produce insulin.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂用工业发酵生产胰岛素。
senses.why: Scaling the sealed jar up to steel tanks turns a kitchen picture into an industrial one.
senses.whyCN: 把密封罐放大成钢制发酵罐，厨房里的画面就被换成了工厂里的画面。

senses.title: Dough fermentation in baking
senses.definition: the rising of dough caused by yeast producing gas inside it
senses.definitionCN: 酵母在面团内部产生气体而使面团膨胀的过程
senses.example: Good bread depends on slow fermentation of the dough.
senses.exampleCN: 好面包取决于面团的缓慢发酵。
senses.why: In dough the gas of the core image becomes bubbles that lift the whole mass upward.
senses.whyCN: 在面团里，核心意象中的气体变成气泡，把整块面团向上托举起来。

senses.title: Fermentation as preservation
senses.definition: the use of fermentation to keep food safe for a long time by making it acidic or alcoholic
senses.definitionCN: 通过使食物变酸或含酒精而长期保存食物的做法
senses.example: Salt and fermentation kept the winter vegetables edible.
senses.exampleCN: 盐和发酵让冬天的蔬菜得以保存食用。
senses.why: Acid and alcohol push out the microbes that spoil food, so the same process also becomes a way of storing it.
senses.whyCN: 酸与酒精挤走了导致腐败的微生物，于是同一套过程又变成了储存食物的办法。

senses.title: A figurative ferment of ideas
senses.titleCN: 比喻：思想情绪的酝酿骚动
senses.definition: a state of excitement or unrest in which ideas or feelings are actively developing
senses.definitionCN: 思想或情绪活跃发展时所处的兴奋或动荡状态
senses.example: That winter the capital was in a fermentation of new ideas.
senses.exampleCN: 那个冬天，首都处在新思想酝酿的骚动之中。
senses.why: Bubbles rising in a closed jar look like unrest building up, so the word can name social excitement as well.
senses.whyCN: 密闭罐中不断上冒的气泡很像积聚中的动荡，因此这个词也能拿来指社会的兴奋与骚动。

intro.en: Fermentation goes back to Latin fermentum, leaven, and to the verb fermentare, to leaven.
intro.cn: fermentation 上溯拉丁语 fermentum（酵母、酵素）与动词 fermentare（使发酵）。

items.en: Fermentum names leaven, the substance that makes dough rise.
items.cn: fermentum 指酵母、酵素，也就是让面团发起来的物质。

items.en: Fermentare is the verb meaning to leaven or to ferment.
items.cn: fermentare 是动词，意为使发酵、使发起来。

items.en: Fermentatio names the act of fermenting.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 fermentatio 指发酵这一动作。

items.en: Old French fermenter carries the verb onward.
items.cn: 古法语 fermenter 把动词继续传下去。

items.en: Middle English ferment names both the agent and the process.
items.cn: 中古英语 ferment 兼指酵素与发酵过程。

items.en: Modern English adds the noun fermentation for the process and for the industry built on it.
items.cn: 现代英语加上名词 fermentation，用来指过程以及建立在它之上的产业。

note.en: Fermentation is the noun of a bubbling transformation, close to ferment and to the words of brewing and souring.
note.cn: fermentation 是「冒泡转化」的名词，与 ferment 以及酿造、变酸一类词相邻。

entries.definition: to break sugar down by microbes, or the agent that causes this
entries.definitionCN: 使糖发酵，也指引起发酵的酵素

entries.definition: able to cause fermentation
a tank or organism in which fermentation happens
entries.definitionCN: 发酵罐；进行发酵的微生物

entries.definition: the making of beer by steeping and fermenting grain
the raising of dough by yeast or another raising agent
preserving food in brine or acid
entries.definitionCN: 腌渍；用盐水或酸液保存食物

normalIntro.en: Fermentation is a jar that seems to work by itself: microbes do the stirring while the lid stays shut.
normalIntro.cn: fermentation 是一只看似自己在工作的罐子：微生物替人搅拌，盖子始终关着。

normal.en: The fermentation process turns sugar into alcohol or acid.
normal.cn: fermentation process 把糖变成酒精或酸。

normal.en: A fermentation tank is where microbes work at industrial scale.
normal.cn: fermentation tank 是微生物大规模工作的地方。

normal.en: Alcoholic fermentation gives wine and beer their strength.
normal.cn: alcoholic fermentation 给葡萄酒和啤酒带来酒精度。

normal.en: Lactic acid fermentation makes yogurt and kimchi sour.
normal.cn: lactic acid fermentation 使酸奶与泡菜变酸。

normal.en: Dough needs slow fermentation to rise well.
normal.cn: 面团需要缓慢发酵才能发得好。

abstract.en: See a sealed jar with bubbles climbing the glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一只密封罐，气泡沿着玻璃壁往上爬。

abstract.en: Picture the same jar still working, not yet finished.
abstract.cn: 想象这只罐子仍在工作，还没有结束。

abstract.en: Think of yeast quietly turning sweet juice into wine.
abstract.cn: 想象酵母悄悄把甜果汁变成葡萄酒。

examples.en: Fermentation gives cheese its sharp taste.
examples.cn: 发酵赋予奶酪浓烈的味道。

examples.en: The winery controls the fermentation temperature closely.
examples.cn: 酒庄密切控制发酵温度。

examples.en: Without fermentation, the dough would stay flat.
examples.cn: 没有发酵，面团就发不起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fer + men + tation」——一群人（men）守在罐边，慢慢等它冒泡；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 fermentum（酵母、酵素）→ fermentare（使发酵）→ 晚期拉丁语 fermentatio → 古法语 fermenter → 英语 fermentation，核心义「让糖在密闭中自行转化」。

sensesIntro.en: Fermentation starts as a microbe-driven process, then spreads to its ongoing state, to brewing and sour food, to industry and baking, to preservation, and finally to a figurative ferment.
sensesIntro.cn: fermentation 从微生物驱动的过程出发，再扩展到进行中的状态、酿酒与酸味食品、工业与烘焙、保存手段，最后落到比喻性的骚动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed jar where sugar bubbles into alcohol or acid.
core.cn: 核心意象：密封罐里的糖冒泡变成酒精或酸。

branches.en: The basic microbial process is the first sense.
branches.cn: 最基本的微生物过程是第 1 个义项。

branches.en: The process seen as an ongoing state is the second sense.
branches.cn: 把过程看作正在进行的状态，是第 2 个义项。

branches.en: Alcohol and acid are the two products that fill the jar image.
branches.cn: 酒精与酸是填满罐中画面的两种产物。

branches.en: Steel tanks and rising dough are the same image at two scales.
branches.cn: 钢制发酵罐与发起来的面团，是同一画面在两种尺度上的样子。

branches.en: Preservation and social ferment both grow from bubbles that will not stay still.
branches.cn: 保存食物与社会的骚动，都从不肯安静的气泡里长出来。

intro.en: Fermentation is built on the Latin leaven word, with English ferment, fermenter, and fermentative around it.
intro.cn: fermentation 由拉丁语中表示「酵母」的词构成，周围有英语 ferment、fermenter 与 fermentative。

latinIntro.en: Latin fermentum means leaven, and fermentare means to leaven.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fermentum 意为酵母、酵素，fermentare 意为使发酵。

items.example: Fermentum is the substance that raises dough.
items.exampleCN: fermentum 是让面团发起来的物质。

items.example: Fermentare gives the English verb.
items.exampleCN: fermentare 提供了英语动词。

items.example: Fermentatio is the direct source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: fermentatio 是英语名词的直接来源。

items.example: Ferment is the short English verb.
items.exampleCN: ferment 是简短的英语动词。

items.example: Fermentation names the process itself.
items.exampleCN: fermentation 指过程本身。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation turns verbs into process nouns.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 把动词变成表示过程的名词。

items.example: Fermentative adds the suffix -ative.
items.exampleCN: fermentative 加上词尾 -ative。

items.example: The suffix -ative marks a tendency.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ative 表示一种倾向。

items.meaning: a vessel or microbe that ferments
items.example: Fermenter adds the suffix -er.
items.exampleCN: fermenter 加上词尾 -er。

items.meaning: person or thing that does something
items.meaningCN: 表示施动者或器具的词尾
items.example: The suffix -er names the doer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 指施动者或器具。

definition_zh: 蕨；蕨类植物；蕨叶
definition_en: a flowerless plant with feathery leaves that reproduces by spores instead of seeds
core_image: 一根绿色羽毛从紧卷的小卷里慢慢展开
scene: 雨后的坡地上，一片羽状的叶子正从卷曲中慢慢舒展开来。The fern had pushed its first frond through the wet soil.
sceneCN: 这里 fern 是「蕨类植物」（第 1 个义项：没有花、叶片羽状、靠孢子繁殖的植物）；句意：那株蕨已经把第一片叶子顶出了湿润的泥土。

derivatives.zh: 多蕨的；蕨状的，由 fern 加后缀 -y 构成
蕨类栽培园；蕨丛，由 fern 加后缀 -ery 构成
像蕨一样的，由 fern 与 like 复合而成

senses.title: A fern as a kind of plant
senses.definition: a flowerless plant with feathery leaves that reproduces by spores rather than by seeds
senses.definitionCN: 一种没有花、叶片羽状、靠孢子而不是种子繁殖的植物
senses.example: The fern in the corner of the garden spreads by spores, not seeds.
senses.exampleCN: 花园角落的那株蕨靠孢子繁殖，而不是靠种子。
senses.why: The core image is a feathery leaf unfolding from a tight coil, which is what a fern looks like as it grows.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是从紧卷中展开的羽状叶片，而蕨长出来时正是这副样子。

senses.title: One fern plant
senses.definition: a single plant of this kind, counted as one individual
senses.definitionCN: 作为单个植株计数的蕨
senses.example: She planted three ferns beside the shaded wall.
senses.exampleCN: 她在背阴的墙边种了三株蕨。
senses.why: From the name of the kind the word moves to countable plants that can be planted one by one.
senses.whyCN: 从「这一类植物」的统称，扩展到可以一株一株栽下的个体，于是有了可数的用法。

senses.title: A fern frond
senses.definition: one of the long feathery leaves of a fern, often used in decoration
senses.definitionCN: 蕨类植物长而羽状的叶片，常用于装饰
senses.example: A single fern frond looks like a green feather.
senses.exampleCN: 一片蕨叶看上去就像一根绿色的羽毛。
senses.why: The long feathery leaf is the part people point at when they name the plant, so the leaf takes the name too.
senses.whyCN: 人们指着这株植物时，说出的是那片长而羽状的叶子，于是叶子也借用了这个名字。

senses.title: A clump of ferns
senses.definition: a dense group of ferns covering the ground in damp shade
senses.definitionCN: 阴湿处铺满地面的一丛丛蕨
senses.example: The forest floor was covered with fern and moss.
senses.exampleCN: 森林地面上覆满了蕨与苔藓。
senses.why: Many fronds packed together make the green carpet that a single leaf only hints at.
senses.whyCN: 许多叶片挤在一起，就成了单片叶子只能暗示的那块绿色地毯。

senses.title: A garden or house fern
senses.definition: a fern grown deliberately for ornament in gardens, pots, or conservatories
senses.definitionCN: 为观赏而栽种在花园、花盆或温室里的蕨
senses.example: Boston fern is a popular house fern for hanging baskets.
senses.exampleCN: 波士顿蕨是吊篮里常见的室内观赏蕨。
senses.why: The feathery shape that pleases the eye turns the wild plant into a decorative object.
senses.whyCN: 赏心悦目的羽状外形，让这种野生植物变成了供人观赏的物件。

senses.title: A fossil fern
senses.definition: a fern preserved in rock, especially those that formed coal beds
senses.definitionCN: 保存在岩石中的蕨类，尤指形成煤层的那些
senses.example: A fossil fern was pressed into the dark shale.
senses.exampleCN: 一片化石蕨被压进了深色页岩。
senses.why: Ferns are ancient plants, so their prints in stone extend the leaf image backwards in time.
senses.whyCN: 蕨是很古老的植物，它们在石头上的印痕把这片叶子的画面往时间深处延伸。

senses.title: A fern as an emblem or pattern
senses.definition: a fern used as a national symbol or as a repeated decorative motif
senses.definitionCN: 被用作国家象征或反复出现的装饰母题的蕨
senses.example: The silver fern appears on jerseys and on the national emblem.
senses.exampleCN: 银蕨出现在球衣与国徽上。
senses.why: A single frond can stand for a whole country or repeat across cloth and carving.
senses.whyCN: 一片蕨叶可以代表整个国家，也可以在织物与雕刻上反复排列。

senses.title: Edible fern shoots
senses.definition: the young coiled shoots of some ferns, eaten as a vegetable
senses.definitionCN: 某些蕨类幼嫩卷曲的芽，可作蔬菜食用
senses.example: In spring people gather fern shoots for a bitter green dish.
senses.exampleCN: 春天人们采蕨芽做一道带苦味的青菜。
senses.why: The coiled young frond of the core image is exactly what cooks pick and boil.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象里卷曲的幼叶，正是厨师采摘下锅的那个东西。

intro.en: Fern descends from Old English fearn, from a Germanic word for the plant.
intro.cn: fern 源自英语 fearn（古英语），其更早形式见于日耳曼语。

items.en: A reconstructed root with the sense of feather or wing may lie behind the word.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个带有「羽毛、翼」意味的重新构拟词根位于这个词的更早层。

items.en: The Germanic form names the fern and passes into Old English.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式指蕨，并传入古英语。

items.en: Fearn names the plant in Old English verse and records.
items.cn: 古英语 fearn 在诗文与记录中指这种植物。

items.en: Middle English settles on fern as the modern spelling approaches.
items.cn: 中古英语固定为 fern，现代拼写由此而来。

items.en: Modern English keeps fern for the plant, its leaf, and its ornamental uses.
items.cn: 现代英语用 fern 指这种植物、它的叶片以及观赏用途。

note.en: Fern names a feathery spore plant, close to its own derivatives and to bracken, moss, and frond.
note.cn: fern 指一种羽状的孢子植物，与本族派生词以及欧洲蕨、苔藓、蕨叶相邻。

entries.definition: full of ferns, or shaped like a fern
a place where ferns are grown
resembling a fern in shape
a large coarse fern that covers open ground
entries.definitionCN: 欧洲蕨；大片生长的大形蕨

entries.definition: a small soft green plant without flowers that grows in damp places
entries.definitionCN: 苔藓；阴湿处的小型绿色植物

entries.definition: the long leaf of a fern or a palm

normalIntro.en: Fern is a leaf shaped like a feather, curling out of the ground without any flower.
normalIntro.cn: fern 是一片像羽毛的叶子，从地里卷着展开，从来不长花。

normal.en: A fern frond looks like a green feather.
normal.cn: fern frond 看上去像一根绿色羽毛。

normal.en: Ferns grow in damp shade, not in dry sun.
normal.cn: 蕨长在阴湿处，而不是干燥的阳光下。

normal.en: Ferns spread by spores rather than by seeds.
normal.cn: 蕨靠孢子而不是种子传播。

normal.en: The silver fern is a symbol of New Zealand.
normal.cn: silver fern 是新西兰的象征。

normal.en: Boston fern is a common houseplant.
normal.cn: Boston fern 是常见的室内盆栽。

abstract.en: Watch a tight green coil slowly open into a feather.
abstract.cn: 想象一个紧卷的绿色小卷慢慢张开成一片羽毛。

abstract.en: Picture one fern standing alone by a shaded wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一株蕨单独立在背阴的墙边。

abstract.en: See a single frond held like a green feather in the hand.
abstract.cn: 想象手里拿着一片像绿色羽毛的蕨叶。

examples.en: Ferns need shade and steady moisture.
examples.cn: 蕨需要阴凉和稳定的湿度。

examples.en: A fern unfurled its first frond in the pot.
examples.cn: 一株蕨在花盆里展开了第一片叶子。

examples.en: The hillside was green with fern and moss.
examples.cn: 山坡上长满蕨与苔藓，一片翠绿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛恩」——蕨叶像一片片小羽毛，仿佛带着「佛恩」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 fearn（蕨）→ 中古英语 fern → 现代英语 fern；更早可上溯日耳曼语 *farnaz，一般认为与「羽毛、翼」的古老词根有关，细节仍有争议。

sensesIntro.en: Fern begins as the plant itself, then its single plant, its frond, its clump, its garden use, its fossil record, its emblem use, and its edible shoots.
sensesIntro.cn: fern 从这种植物本身出发，依次指单株、叶片、蕨丛、园林用途、化石记录、标志用途与可食的蕨芽。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a green feather unrolling from a tight coil.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根绿色羽毛从紧卷中展开。

branches.en: The plant itself is the primary sense.
branches.cn: 这种植物本身是首要义项。

branches.en: A counted single plant follows from the name of the kind.
branches.cn: 可数的单株是从「这一类」的名称里分出来的。

branches.en: The frond is both the leaf and the food people gather.
branches.cn: 蕨叶既是那片子，也是人们采来吃的菜。

branches.en: Clumps and garden planting extend the leaf into landscape.
branches.cn: 蕨丛与园林栽种把这片叶子扩展成了景观。

branches.en: Stone prints and national emblems carry the frond beyond the garden.
branches.cn: 石头上的印痕与国徽上的图案，把蕨叶带出了花园。

intro.en: Fern comes from Old English fearn, and English builds ferny, fernery, and fernlike on it.
intro.cn: fern 来自古英语 fearn，英语在它之上构成 ferny、fernery 与 fernlike。

latinIntro.en: Latin names the fern filix, a word of unrelated origin that supplies many botanical terms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把蕨称作 filix，这个词与英语 fern 不同源，却提供了许多植物学名称。

items.example: Fearn is the Old English name of the plant.
items.exampleCN: fearn 是这种植物的古英语名称。

items.meaning: a spore-bearing plant with feathery leaves
items.example: Fern keeps the plant sense.
items.exampleCN: fern 保留植物义。

items.example: Ferns is the regular plural.
items.exampleCN: ferns 是规则复数。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.meaningCN: 充满……的；具有……性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -y forms ferny.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 ferny。

items.meaning: full of ferns, or like a fern
items.example: Ferny describes a shaded bank.
items.exampleCN: ferny 形容长满蕨的背阴坡地。

items.example: The suffix -ery forms fernery.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ery 构成 fernery。

items.meaning: a place where ferns are grown
items.example: Fernery names a fern garden.
items.exampleCN: fernery 指种蕨的园子。

items.meaning: fern, the Latin name of the plant
items.example: Filix is the Latin word for fern.
items.exampleCN: filix 是拉丁语里的蕨。

items.meaning: the stem of filix, used in compounds
items.example: The stem filic- appears in botanical names.
items.exampleCN: 词干 filic- 出现在植物学名称里。

definition_zh: 雪貂；用雪貂狩猎；翻找；查获
definition_en: a small tame animal with a long body, kept for hunting rabbits or as a pet, and a verb meaning to search persistently
core_image: 一只细长的身子钻进洞穴，把藏着的猎物赶了出来
scene: 猎人在洞口蹲下，屏住呼吸等着洞里的动静。The ferret slipped into the burrow and drove the rabbit out.
sceneCN: 这里 ferret 是「雪貂」（第 1 个义项：身体细长、用于狩猎或作宠物的小型家养动物）；句意：雪貂钻进洞穴，把兔子赶了出来。

derivatives.zh: 雪貂似的；爱打探的，由 ferret 加后缀 -y 构成
用雪貂狩猎的人；打探者，由 ferret 加后缀 -er 构成

senses.title: A ferret as a tame animal
senses.definition: a small tame animal with a long body, short legs, and a pointed face, kept for hunting or as a pet
senses.definitionCN: 一种身体细长、腿短、脸尖的小型家养动物，用于狩猎或作宠物
senses.example: The ferret slept in a hammock inside its cage.
senses.exampleCN: 那只雪貂睡在笼子里的吊床上。
senses.why: The core image is a narrow body slipping into a burrow, and that body is the animal itself.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一个细长的身子钻进洞穴，而这个身子正是雪貂本身。

senses.title: Hunting with ferrets
senses.definition: the sport of sending ferrets into burrows to drive rabbits or rats out into nets
senses.definitionCN: 把雪貂送进洞穴，把兔子或老鼠赶进网里的狩猎活动
senses.example: Ferreting is still practised in some rural counties.
senses.exampleCN: 在一些乡下地区，用雪貂狩猎仍有人在干。
senses.why: A tame ferret follows a burrow that a dog cannot enter, so the animal turns into a method.
senses.whyCN: 驯养的雪貂能钻进狗进不去的洞，于是这只动物本身变成了一种打猎方法。

senses.title: To search by rummaging
senses.definition: to search for something by opening drawers, pockets, or piles and looking through them
senses.definitionCN: 通过翻抽屉、口袋或成堆的东西来寻找某物
senses.example: She ferreted through the drawer for her passport.
senses.exampleCN: 她翻遍抽屉找她的护照。
senses.why: The animal twists through narrow tunnels, and the verb copies that movement through clutter.
senses.whyCN: 雪貂在狭窄的洞道里扭身穿行，动词就把这个动作搬到了杂乱的物件之间。

senses.title: To ferret out a fact
senses.definition: to discover something hidden by persistent searching, especially information or wrongdoing
senses.definitionCN: 通过持续查找发现隐藏之物，尤指信息或不当行为
senses.example: Reporters ferreted out the truth about the missing funds.
senses.exampleCN: 记者查出了那笔失踪资金的真相。
senses.why: What the ferret drives out of a hole becomes, in the phrase ferret out, what a searcher drives into the open.
senses.whyCN: 雪貂把猎物从洞里赶出来，在 ferret out 这个说法里，就成了搜寻者把东西赶到明处。

senses.title: To ferret about
senses.definition: to move around a place searching in many small directions, often without a clear plan
senses.definitionCN: 在一个地方来回走动、四处查找，常常没有明确计划
senses.example: He ferreted about in the attic all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 他整个下午在阁楼里到处翻找。
senses.why: The side-to-side movement of a ferret in a tunnel gives the verb its restless, wandering feel.
senses.whyCN: 雪貂在洞道里左右扭动的样子，给了这个动词一种不安分、到处游走的感觉。

senses.title: The ferret as a pet
senses.definition: the keeping of ferrets as household pets, with cages, harnesses, and daily play
senses.definitionCN: 把雪貂当家庭宠物饲养，需要笼子、牵引带与日常玩耍
senses.example: Ferret owners often let their animals sleep most of the day.
senses.exampleCN: 养雪貂的人常常任由它们一天里大半时间睡觉。
senses.why: Because the animal is tame and curious, the same word also names a whole hobby and a corner of the home.
senses.whyCN: 因为这动物温顺又好奇，同一个词也就指一整套饲养爱好与家里的一角。

senses.title: The ferret in the laboratory
senses.definition: a ferret used in medical research, especially in studies of breathing infections
senses.definitionCN: 用于医学研究的雪貂，尤其用于呼吸道感染研究
senses.example: The ferret is a standard model for influenza research.
senses.exampleCN: 雪貂是流感研究的标准模型。
senses.why: Its lungs react much like human lungs, so the tame animal of the core image becomes a scientific instrument.
senses.whyCN: 它的肺反应与人肺相似，于是核心意象里那只温顺动物成了科研工具。

senses.title: A prying person
senses.definition: a person who keeps probing into the private affairs of other people
senses.definitionCN: 不断打探他人私事的人
senses.example: The office ferret knew every rumour before lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室那个爱打探的人午饭前就知道了所有传闻。
senses.why: The hunting habit of driving prey out of hiding turns into a metaphor for a person who digs out secrets.
senses.whyCN: 把猎物从藏身处赶出来的狩猎习惯，转成了「挖出别人秘密」的比喻。

intro.en: Ferret comes through Old French furet, a little thief, from Latin fur, thief.
intro.cn: 一般认为 ferret 经古法语 furet（小贼）而来，上溯拉丁语 fur（小偷）。

items.en: Fur names a thief, and furtum names theft.
items.cn: 拉丁语 fur 指小偷，furtum 指偷窃。

items.en: Furare is the verb meaning to steal.
items.cn: furare 是表示偷窃的动词。

items.en: Old French furet is a diminutive of a word for stealing, so the animal is a little thief.
items.cn: 古法语 furet 是表示「偷窃」的词的小称形式，于是这种动物成了「小贼」。

items.en: Middle English adopts furet as the name of the animal.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 furet，用作这种动物的名称。

items.en: The spelling settles as ferret in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，拼写固定为 ferret。

items.en: Modern English extends ferret from the animal to the act of searching.
items.cn: 现代英语把 ferret 从动物扩展到「搜寻」这一动作。

note.en: Ferret is a narrow-bodied hunter whose name also means to search, close to its own family and to other small hunters.
note.cn: ferret 指一种身体细长的猎手，其名字也表示「搜寻」，与本族词以及其他小型猎手相邻。

entries.definition: like a ferret, or inclined to pry
a person who hunts with ferrets

normalIntro.en: Ferret is a thin animal that goes down a hole and comes back with something.
normalIntro.cn: ferret 是一只细长的动物，钻进洞里，再带着东西出来。

normal.en: Ferret out means to discover something hidden.
normal.cn: ferret out 表示查出隐藏的东西。

normal.en: Ferrets were used to chase rabbits from burrows.
normal.cn: 雪貂曾被用来把兔子从洞里赶出来。

normal.en: A ferret has a long body and short legs.
normal.cn: 雪貂身体长、腿短。

normal.en: She ferreted through the papers for the letter.
normal.cn: 她翻遍文件找那封信。

normal.en: Compare weasel: a ferret is a tame kind of hunter kept by people.
normal.cn: 对比 weasel：ferret 是被人驯养的猎手。

abstract.en: See a narrow body disappearing into a rabbit hole.
abstract.cn: 想象一个细长的身子钻进兔子洞。

abstract.en: Picture a hunter waiting above while the ferret works below.
abstract.cn: 想象猎人在上面等，雪貂在下面干活。

abstract.en: Think of a hand pushing through a crowded drawer.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在塞满东西的抽屉里翻找。

examples.en: Ferrets sleep up to eighteen hours a day.
examples.cn: 雪貂一天最多能睡十八个小时。

examples.en: The team ferreted out the error in the accounts.
examples.cn: 小组查出了账目里的错误。

examples.en: He ferreted about in the cupboard for the missing key.
examples.cn: 他在柜子里到处翻找那把不见的钥匙。

root: 一般认为拉丁语 fur（小偷）→ 古法语 furet（小贼，小称形式）→ 中古英语 furet → 英语 ferret；由「小偷」的机敏形象转为「钻洞搜寻」的动词义。

sensesIntro.en: Ferret starts as the tame animal, then its hunting use, its searching verbs, its pet and laboratory roles, and finally a metaphor for a prying person.
sensesIntro.cn: ferret 从这种驯养动物出发，依次指狩猎用途、搜寻类动词、宠物与实验角色，最后落到「爱打探的人」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long thin body sliding into a burrow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个细长的身子滑进洞穴。

branches.en: The animal is the primary sense.
branches.cn: 这只动物是首要义项。

branches.en: Hunting with the animal is the second sense.
branches.cn: 用它来狩猎是第 2 个义项。

branches.en: The tunnel movement becomes rummaging through clutter.
branches.cn: 在洞道里穿行的动作，变成了在杂物里翻找。

branches.en: Driving hidden things into the open links the search and the prying person.
branches.cn: 把藏起来的东西赶到明处，串起了「查出」与「爱打探的人」。

branches.en: Pet keeping and laboratory use show the tame animal in two modern settings.
branches.cn: 宠物饲养与实验室用途，是这只驯养动物在两种现代场景里的样子。

intro.en: Ferret carries a Latin thief word, and English adds ferrety, ferreter, and the phrasal verb ferret out.
intro.cn: ferret 带着拉丁语「小偷」一词，英语加上 ferrety、ferreter 以及短语动词 ferret out。

latinIntro.en: Latin fur means thief, and furtum means theft.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fur 意为小偷，furtum 意为偷窃。

items.example: Furtum names the act of stealing.

items.example: Ferreting names the activity.
items.exampleCN: ferreting 指这项活动。

items.exampleCN: ferrety 加上词尾 -y。

items.meaning: a person who hunts with ferrets
items.example: Ferreter adds the suffix -er.
items.exampleCN: ferreter 加上词尾 -er。

definition_zh: 渡船；渡轮；渡运；运送
definition_en: a boat that carries people, cars, or goods across a short stretch of water, or to carry them across in such a boat
core_image: 一艘平底船在两岸之间来回滑动，把人与车送到对岸
scene: 清晨的码头上，车辆排着队等船靠岸。The ferry carried the last truck across the river before dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 ferry 是「渡船」（第 1 个义项：把乘客、车辆或货物运过一段水面的船）；句意：天亮前，那艘渡船把最后一辆卡车运过了河。

derivatives.zh: 渡夫；摆渡人，由 ferry 与 man 复合而成
渡船，由 ferry 与 boat 复合而成
渡运费；渡运业，由 ferry 加后缀 -age 构成

senses.title: A ferry as a boat
senses.definition: a boat that carries people, cars, or goods across a short stretch of water
senses.definitionCN: 把乘客、车辆或货物运过一段水面的船
senses.example: The ferry left the harbour with a full load of cars.
senses.exampleCN: 渡轮满载着汽车驶离港口。
senses.why: The core image is a flat boat sliding from one bank to the other, and the boat is what the word first names.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一艘平底船从一岸滑向另一岸，而这个词最先命名的就是那条船。

senses.title: To ferry across water
senses.definition: to carry people or goods across water in a boat
senses.definitionCN: 用船把人或货物运过水面
senses.example: A small boat ferries hikers to the island each morning.
senses.exampleCN: 每天早晨，一只小船把徒步者渡到岛上。
senses.why: The boat and its route collapse into one verb, so that crossing the water becomes the action itself.
senses.whyCN: 船与航线合成一个动词，渡过水面这件事本身就成了那个动作。

senses.title: A ferry service or route
senses.definition: a scheduled service, with boats and a timetable, that links two shores
senses.definitionCN: 由船只与时刻表组成、连接两岸的定期服务
senses.example: The ferry runs every half hour across the strait.
senses.exampleCN: 渡轮每半小时一班横渡海峡。
senses.why: One crossing repeated on a timetable turns a single boat into an institution.
senses.whyCN: 同一次横渡按时刻表一次次重复，一条船就变成了一项固定的服务。

senses.title: The crossing itself
senses.definition: the passage over water between two landing points
senses.definitionCN: 两个靠岸点之间那段水上航程
senses.example: The ferry crossing takes about twenty minutes in calm weather.
senses.exampleCN: 天气平静时，这段渡程大约要二十分钟。
senses.why: The word can name the stretch of water crossed, not only the vessel that crosses it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能指被渡过的那段水面，而不只是渡过它的那条船。

senses.title: Carrying vehicles and freight
senses.definition: to transport cars, trucks, or freight across water on a large vessel
senses.definitionCN: 用大型船只把汽车、卡车或货物运过水面
senses.example: The company ferries trucks across the lake every night.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司每晚把卡车运过湖面。
senses.why: Once the boat carries wheels and containers, the verb grows into heavy transport.
senses.whyCN: 一旦船上装的是车轮与集装箱，这个动词就长成了重型运输。

senses.title: To fly an aircraft to its base
senses.titleCN: 转场；把飞机飞到目的地
senses.definition: to fly an aircraft from one place to another, especially when delivering or repositioning it
senses.definitionCN: 把飞机从一处飞到另一处，尤指交付或调机
senses.example: The pilot ferried the new plane to its home airport.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员把那架新飞机转场飞回基地机场。
senses.why: Air transport copies the sea crossing, because a vehicle is still moved from one point to another.
senses.whyCN: 空运复制了渡海的模式，因为被移动的仍然是一件从一点到另一点的交通工具。

senses.title: To carry back and forth
senses.definition: to carry things repeatedly between two places that are close together
senses.definitionCN: 在相距不远的两个地点之间反复运送东西
senses.example: Volunteers ferried water to the stranded villagers all day.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者整天往受困的村民那里运水。
senses.why: The back-and-forth rhythm of a ferry route becomes any repeated carrying.
senses.whyCN: 渡轮航线上来回往返的节奏，变成了任何反复搬运的动作。

senses.title: The ferry business
senses.definition: the trade or business of operating ferries for passengers and freight
senses.definitionCN: 经营渡船、运送乘客与货物的行业
senses.example: Ferry traffic fell after the bridge opened.
senses.exampleCN: 大桥通车后，渡运业务就衰落了。
senses.why: A boat, a route, and a timetable together form a trade, and the word names that trade too.
senses.whyCN: 船、航线与时刻表合在一起成了一门生意，这个词也指这门生意。

intro.en: Ferry goes back to Old English ferian, to carry, from a Germanic verb meaning to go across.
intro.cn: ferry 上溯古英语 ferian（运送），来自一个意为「渡过去」的日耳曼语动词。

items.en: A reconstructed root for crossing or going over lies behind the family.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个表示「越过、渡过去」的重新构拟词根位于这个词族之后。

items.en: The Germanic verb means to carry or to convey.
items.cn: 日耳曼语动词意为运送、传送。

items.en: Ferian means to carry something from place to place.
items.cn: 古英语 ferian 意为把某物从一处运到另一处。

items.en: Middle English ferien keeps the carrying sense while the water sense grows.
items.cn: 中古英语 ferien 保留运送义，水上渡运的含义则逐渐生长。

items.en: Modern English ferry names the boat, the route, and the carrying trade.
items.cn: 现代英语 ferry 指船、航线与渡运生意。

note.en: Ferry is a carrying word tied to water, close to its compounds and to shuttle, crossing, and boat.
note.cn: ferry 是一个与水面绑定的「运送」词，与它的复合词以及摆渡班车、渡程、小船相邻。

the fare paid for a ferry, or the ferrying trade

normalIntro.cn: ferry 是一艘平底船，在同样的两岸之间来回滑动。

normal.en: Take the ferry to cross the river.
normal.cn: take the ferry 就是乘渡轮过河。

normal.en: A ferry crossing is the short trip over the water.
normal.cn: ferry crossing 是那段短程水上航程。

normal.en: A car ferry carries vehicles, not only people.
normal.cn: car ferry 运的是车辆，不只是人。

normal.en: The verb ferry means to carry people or goods across.

abstract.en: See a flat boat sliding from one bank to the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘平底船从一岸滑向另一岸。

abstract.en: Picture a passenger handing over a ticket at the ramp.
abstract.cn: 想象乘客在跳板处递出一张船票。

abstract.en: Think of a timetable pinned beside the harbour.
abstract.cn: 想象码头边钉着一张时刻表。

examples.cn: 日出前我们乘渡轮过了海湾。

examples.en: The ferry carries cars and foot passengers on the same trip.
examples.cn: 这艘渡轮一趟既运汽车也运步行乘客。

examples.en: They ferried the supplies to the island during the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨期间他们把补给运到了岛上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费里」——坐渡轮要「费力」划到对岸；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 ferian（运送）→ 中古英语 ferien → 现代英语 ferry；一般认为其日耳曼语源与「越过、渡过去」的古老词根有关，因此兼指渡船、渡运与渡口生意。

sensesIntro.en: Ferry begins with the boat, turns into the act of carrying across water, then the service, the crossing, heavy freight, aircraft delivery, repeated carrying, and the trade itself.
sensesIntro.cn: ferry 从渡船开始，转为「渡运」的动作，再到航线服务、渡程、重型货运、飞机转场、反复搬运，最后是渡运生意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat boat sliding between two banks.
core.cn: 核心意象：一艘平底船在两岸之间来回滑动。

branches.en: The boat itself is the primary sense.
branches.cn: 那条船本身是首要义项。

branches.en: Carrying across water and carrying back and forth are the two verb senses.
branches.cn: 渡水运送与来回搬运，是两个动词义项。

branches.en: A repeated crossing makes both a service and a named stretch of water.
branches.cn: 反复的横渡既造出一项服务，也造出一段有了名字的水面。

branches.en: Trucks and aircraft show the same carrying image with engines.
branches.cn: 卡车与飞机，是同一幅运送画面换上了发动机。

branches.en: Boat, route, and timetable together become a trade.
branches.cn: 船、航线与时刻表合在一起，就成了一门生意。

intro.en: Ferry is an Old English carrying verb, with ferryman, ferryboat, and ferriage built from it.
intro.cn: ferry 是古英语的「运送」动词，英语由它构成 ferryman、ferryboat 与 ferriage。

latinIntro.en: Ferry has no Latin source, and Latin portare, to carry, is only a meaning neighbour.
latinIntro.cn: ferry 没有拉丁语来源，拉丁语 portare（搬运）只是意义相近的邻词。

items.exampleCN: ferrying 指渡运这件事。

items.meaning: a person who does a job
items.meaningCN: 表示从事某职业者的词尾

definition_zh: 渡船；渡轮；摆渡船
definition_en: a boat that carries people, and often vehicles, across a short stretch of water
core_image: 一艘平底小船在两岸之间来回摆渡，把人和车送到对岸
scene: 傍晚的码头起了薄雾，乘客提着行李排队等最后一班船。The last ferryboat of the day came in with a low rumble.
sceneCN: 这里 ferryboat 是「渡船」（第 1 个义项：载人过短程水面的小船）；句意：当天最后一班渡船伴着低沉的轰鸣靠岸。

derivatives.zh: 由古英语动词转成的名词，指渡船或渡运服务，是 ferryboat 的中心词
ferry 加 man，指在渡口撑船摆渡的人
ferry 加 -age，指渡运或渡船费，现已少用

senses.title: A boat that carries passengers across water
senses.definition: a boat used to take passengers from one shore to the other over a short distance
senses.definitionCN: 用于把乘客从一岸送到另一岸的短程小船
senses.example: We took a ferryboat across the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 我们乘渡船穿过港湾。
senses.why: Ferry comes from an Old English verb meaning to carry, so the boat is simply the carrier.
senses.whyCN: ferry 源自表示「运送」的古英语动词，所以这条船就是「运送者」本身。

senses.title: A boat built to carry vehicles
senses.definition: a ferryboat with a wide deck that cars and lorries can drive onto
senses.definitionCN: 甲板宽大、汽车和卡车可以直接开上去的渡船
senses.example: The car ferryboat holds thirty lorries at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘车辆渡轮一次能装三十辆卡车。
senses.why: Once the word named the carrying act, a boat with a drive-on deck naturally took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本指「运送」这个动作，能开上车的宽甲板船自然沿用了同一个名字。

senses.title: A vessel on a fixed shuttle route
senses.titleCN: 班次渡船；定点往返的渡船
senses.definition: the boat of a regular service that shuttles to a timetable between two points
senses.definitionCN: 按时刻表在两点之间定点往返的班船
senses.example: The island ferryboat leaves every hour on the hour.
senses.exampleCN: 岛上的班次渡船每逢整点开一班。
senses.why: A ferry is also a service, so the vessel that keeps to its timetable is called a ferryboat too.
senses.whyCN: ferry 也指渡运服务，因此按时刻表往返的那条船同样叫 ferryboat。

intro.en: Ferryboat joins ferry, from Old English ferian, to carry across, with boat, from Old English bat.
intro.cn: ferryboat 由 ferry（源自古英语 ferian，意为运送过水）与 boat（源自古英语 bat，意为小船）复合而成。

items.en: The reconstructed verb farjan means to carry or convey.
items.cn: 重构的动词 farjan 意为运送、载运。

items.en: Ferian means to carry, convey, or ferry someone across water.
items.cn: ferian 意为运送、载人过水。

items.en: Bat names a small vessel, a word later spelled boat.
items.cn: bat 指小船，这个词后来拼作 boat。

items.en: Ferien and bot combine in the sense of a carrying boat.
items.cn: ferien 与 bot 组合，指用来运送的船。

items.en: Ferryboat is recorded as one word for a boat that ferries passengers.
items.cn: ferryboat 作为一个词被记录下来，指载客摆渡的船。

items.en: Modern ferries add vehicle decks, timetables, and island routes.
items.cn: 现代渡船增加了车辆甲板、时刻表与海岛航线。

note.en: Ferryboat belongs to the ferry family and sits close to other words for short water crossings.
note.cn: ferryboat 属于 ferry 词族，与表示短程过水的其他词相邻。

carried across water in the past
